docString:
Pointwise data for differentiating a finite orthonormal eigenbasis in indexed parameter
directions.

All directions share the same Hamiltonian, eigenbasis, and spectrum. The differentiated eigenpair
and orthonormality identities are stored directionwise. No self-adjointness assumption is imposed
on the Hamiltonian derivatives here; results that need it state it separately.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData κ ι H)
  [inst_4 : DecidableEq ι] (μ ν : κ) (n : ι),
  (∀ (ρ : κ), IsSelfAdjoint (data.hamiltonianDerivative ρ)) →
    (∀ (m : ι), m ≠ n → data.energy m ≠ data.energy n) →
      data.berryCurvature μ ν n =
        ∑ m,
          if m = n then 0
          else
            2 *
              (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement μ m n / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m) *
                  (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement ν n m / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m))).im
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.berryCurvature_eq_sum_hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElements
docString:
Force/Hamiltonian-derivative matrix-element representation of Berry curvature for a
nondegenerate band.

This is the finite-dimensional pointwise formula needed by the clean anomalous-Hall consumer.
Self-adjointness of all directional Hamiltonian derivatives is an explicit hypothesis.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData κ ι H) (μ ν : κ)
  (n : ι),
  data.berryCurvature μ ν n =
    ∑ m,
      -2 *
        (inner ℂ (data.eigenvectorDerivative μ n) (data.eigenbasis m) *
            inner ℂ (data.eigenbasis m) (data.eigenvectorDerivative ν n)).im

docString:
Completeness of the finite orthonormal eigenbasis expands the derivative-state curvature into

docString: Berry curvature is antisymmetric in its two parameter directions.

Born--Fock off-diagonal eigenvector-derivative formula in parameter direction `μ`.

The nondegeneracy needed for division by the level spacing is an explicit theorem hypothesis rather

name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.ofSimpleSpectrum
docString:
Construct pointwise differentiated eigenbasis data from a simple finite spectrum.

The simple-spectrum hypothesis is expressed by injectivity of the band-energy map.
Energy derivatives are the lossless diagonal expectations of the self-adjoint Hamiltonian
derivatives. Eigenvector derivatives are constructed algebraically in the parallel-transport gauge
`⟪φ_n, ∂_μ φ_n⟫ = 0`, so a concrete model need not differentiate an explicit eigenvector gauge.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (hamiltonian : H →L[ℂ] H),
  IsSelfAdjoint hamiltonian →
    ∀ (eigenbasis : OrthonormalBasis ι ℂ H) (energy : ι → ℝ),
      (∀ (n : ι), hamiltonian (eigenbasis n) = ↑(energy n) • eigenbasis n) →
        ∀ (hamiltonianDerivative : κ → H →L[ℂ] H)
          (hamiltonianDerivative_selfAdjoint : ∀ (μ : κ), IsSelfAdjoint (hamiltonianDerivative μ)),
          Function.Injective energy →
            ∀ (μ : κ) (n : ι),
              (hamiltonianDerivative μ) (eigenbasis n) +
                  hamiltonian
                    (BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.simpleSpectrumEigenvectorDerivative✝ eigenbasis energy
                      hamiltonianDerivative μ n) =
                ↑((hamiltonianDerivative μ).diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (eigenbasis n)) • eigenbasis n +
                  ↑(energy n) •
                    BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.simpleSpectrumEigenvectorDerivative✝ eigenbasis energy
                      hamiltonianDerivative μ n
name: BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.ofSimpleSpectrum._proof_1

  (hamiltonianDerivative : κ → H →L[ℂ] H),
  (∀ (μ : κ), IsSelfAdjoint (hamiltonianDerivative μ)) →
    Function.Injective energy →
      ∀ (μ : κ) (m n : ι),
        inner ℂ
              (BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.simpleSpectrumEigenvectorDerivative✝ eigenbasis energy
                hamiltonianDerivative μ m)
              (eigenbasis n) +
            inner ℂ (eigenbasis m)
              (BerryGeometry.PointwiseEigenbasisData.simpleSpectrumEigenvectorDerivative✝ eigenbasis energy
                hamiltonianDerivative μ n) =
          0

    PSigma.casesOn _x fun m n =>
      match m, n with
      | 0, n => Fintype.ofEquiv Unit (Combinatorics.BinaryShuffle.zeroLeftEquiv n).symm
      | m.succ, 0 => Fintype.ofEquiv Unit (Combinatorics.BinaryShuffle.zeroRightEquiv (m + 1)).symm
      | m.succ, n.succ =>
        Fintype.ofEquiv (Combinatorics.BinaryShuffle m (n + 1) ⊕ Combinatorics.BinaryShuffle (m + 1) n)

    | m.succ, 0 => Fintype.ofEquiv Unit (Combinatorics.BinaryShuffle.zeroRightEquiv (m + 1)).symm
    | m.succ, n.succ =>

ambient pairing agrees with selecting the corresponding endpoint of the decomposed normalized
pair.

    {k ∈ {k ∈ Finset.Ioo 0 (pairing.partner 0) | pairing.partner k < pairing.partner 0} | k < pairing.partner k}.card =

  (componentPairEquiv : (B : ι) × (componentPairing B).NormalizedPair ≃ global.NormalizedPair) (weight factor : R)
  (localWeight : ι → R) (pairValue : Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n) → R)
  (localPairValue : (B : ι) → Fin (2 * m B) → Fin (2 * m B) → R),
  weight = factor * ∏ B, localWeight B →
    (∀ (B : ι) (pr : (componentPairing B).NormalizedPair),
        pairValue (↑(componentPairEquiv ⟨B, pr⟩)).1 (↑(componentPairEquiv ⟨B, pr⟩)).2 =
          localPairValue B (↑pr).1 (↑pr).2) →

  (pairValue : Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n) → R) (localPairValue : (B : ι) → Fin (2 * m B) → Fin (2 * m B) → R),

      pairValue (↑(componentPairEquiv ⟨B, pr⟩)).1 (↑(componentPairEquiv ⟨B, pr⟩)).2 =

  (∀ (pr : P.NormalizedPair),
      value (↑((Combinatorics.Pairing.ofSplitNormalizedPairEquiv e P Q) (Sum.inl pr))).1
          (↑((Combinatorics.Pairing.ofSplitNormalizedPairEquiv e P Q) (Sum.inl pr))).2 =

a multiplicative connected decomposition, then the factorial-normalized formal-log coefficient is
the connected contribution.  The proof factors through the equality of the two replica
polynomials, not through cumulant inversion.

      s ≠ ∅ →
        ↑s.card.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff s.card) Z.logOf =
          Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment (fun T => ↑T.card.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff T.card) Z) s

positions, the crossing-weighted pairing sum reduces to the cycle-weighted permutation sum of the
side-oriented matrix, up to the factor fixed by the side splitting. The involutive hypothesis is
needed only to identify crossing parity with permutation cycle parity.

statement: {ι : Type u_1} → [Fintype ι] → ℂ → Matrix ι ι ℂ → PowerSeries ℂ
name: Combinatorics.permutationConnectedCycleSeries
docString:
The formal connected-cycle series associated with exchange weight `ζ` and finite kernel `K`.

Its constant coefficient is zero. At positive order `m`, its coefficient is the EGF-normalized
assignment-summed one-cycle contribution.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] (ζ : ℂ) (w : ι → ℂ),
  ζ ≠ 0 →
    Combinatorics.permutationConnectedCycleSeries ζ (Matrix.diagonal w) =
      -ζ⁻¹ • ∑ i, (PowerSeries.rescale (-ζ * w i)) (PowerSeries.log ℂ)
name: Combinatorics.permutationConnectedCycleSeries_diagonal_eq_neg_inv_smul_sum_log
docString:
For a diagonal kernel and nonzero exchange weight, the connected-cycle series is the scaled sum
of the modewise formal logarithms `log(1 - ζ wᵢ t)`.

statement: {α : Type u_1} → [DecidableEq α] → [Fintype α] → {R : Type u_2} → [CommSemiring R] → R → (α → α → R) → Finset α → R
name: Combinatorics.permutationSum
docString:
The arbitrary-`ζ` permutation sum on a finite support set. This is the sole project-local
permutation-sum backend; the weight is instantiated through the generic connected-decomposition
machinery rather than maintained as a separate direct sum.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {inst : DecidableEq α} [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] [inst_2 : Fintype α] {R : Type u_2}
  [inst_3 : CommSemiring R] (ζ ζ_1 : R),
  ζ = ζ_1 →
    ∀ (K K_1 : α → α → R),
      K = K_1 →
        ∀ (S S_1 : Finset α), S = S_1 → Combinatorics.permutationSum ζ K S = Combinatorics.permutationSum ζ_1 K_1 S_1
name: Combinatorics.permutationSum.congr_simp

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Fintype α] {R : Type u_2} [inst_2 : CommSemiring R] (ζ : R)
  (K : α → α → R) (S : Finset α),
  Combinatorics.permutationSum ζ K S = (Combinatorics.permutationMultiplicativeWeight✝ ζ K).objectMoment S
name: Combinatorics.permutationSum.eq_1

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Fintype α] {R : Type u_2} [inst_2 : CommSemiring R] (ζ : R)
  (K : α → α → R) (S : Finset α),
  Combinatorics.permutationSum ζ K S = Finpartition.momentFromCumulant (Combinatorics.singleCycleContribution ζ K) S
name: Combinatorics.permutationSum_eq_momentFromCumulant
docString: The arbitrary-`ζ` permutation sum is the moment transform of the single-cycle contribution.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Fintype α] {R : Type u_2} [inst_2 : CommSemiring R] (ζ : R)
  (K : α → α → R), Combinatorics.permutationSum ζ K Finset.univ = ∑ σ, ζ ^ Combinatorics.cycleDefect σ * ∏ i, K i (σ i)
name: Combinatorics.permutationSum_univ_eq_sum_perm
docString:
On the full finite index type, the connected-decomposition backend is the usual direct sum over
all permutations with weight `ζ ^ cycleDefect`. This is the bridge consumed by the perfect-pairing
reduction; it is not a second backend.

statement: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Monoid R] {ζ : R}, ζ * ζ = 1 → ∀ {a b : ℕ}, a % 2 = b % 2 → ζ ^ a = ζ ^ b
name: Combinatorics.pow_eq_of_mod_two_eq
docString: A power of an involutive scalar (`ζ * ζ = 1`) only depends on the exponent's parity.

statement: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : CommRing R] → [Algebra ℚ R] → PowerSeries R → ℕ → R
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff
docString: The exponential-generating-function normalization of a formal-log coefficient.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Algebra ℚ R] (Z : PowerSeries R) (n : ℕ),
  Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff Z n = ↑n.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff n) Z.logOf
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff.eq_1

statement:
∀ {Z : PowerSeries ℂ},
  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 →
    Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff Z 1 = Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z 1
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff_one_eq
docString: The first cumulant coefficient equals the first moment coefficient.

statement:
∀ {Z : PowerSeries ℂ},
  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 →
    Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff Z 3 =
      Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z 3 -
          3 * Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z 1 * Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z 2 +
        2 * Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z 1 ^ 3
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff_three_eq
docString: The third cumulant coefficient removes all one-plus-two and three-singleton decompositions.

statement:
∀ {Z : PowerSeries ℂ},
  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 →
    Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff Z 2 =
      Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z 2 - Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z 1 ^ 2
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff_two_eq
docString: The second cumulant coefficient subtracts the disconnected product of two first moments.

statement: {R : Type u_1} → [Semiring R] → PowerSeries R → ℕ → R
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff
docString: The exponential-generating-function normalization of a power-series coefficient.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (Z : PowerSeries R) (n : ℕ),
  Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z n = ↑n.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff n) Z
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff.eq_1

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Algebra ℚ R] {Z : PowerSeries R},
  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 →
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z (n + 1) =
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          ↑(n.choose k) * Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff Z (k + 1) *
            Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z (n - k)
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff_succ_recurrence
docString:
The factorial-normalized moment and formal-log coefficients satisfy the triangular
moment-cumulant recurrence.

{α : Type u_1} →

    [inst : Semiring R] →
      (Z : PowerSeries R) → PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 → Combinatorics.NormalizedSetFunction α R
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentSetFunction
docString:
Factorial-normalized coefficients of a unit-constant power series, bundled as normalized
finite-set moment data.

∀ {α : Type u_2} {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (Z : PowerSeries R),
  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 → Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z ∅.card = 1
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentSetFunction._proof_1

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (Z Z_1 : PowerSeries R) (e_Z : Z = Z_1)
  (hZ : PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1),
  Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentSetFunction Z hZ = Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentSetFunction Z_1 ⋯
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentSetFunction.congr_simp

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (Z : PowerSeries R) (hZ : PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1)
  (M : Combinatorics.NormalizedSetFunction α R),
  Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentSetFunction Z hZ = M ↔
    ∀ (S : Finset α), Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff Z S.card = M.toFun S
name: Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentSetFunction_eq_iff
docString:
Equality of the bundled power-series moment function with normalized finite-set moment data is
equivalent to equality of the factorial-normalized coefficients on every finite set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Field R] [CharZero R] {Z : PowerSeries R},
  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 →
    ∀ (s : Finset α) (k : ℕ),
      ↑s.card.factorial / ↑k.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff s.card) ((Z - 1) ^ k) =
        ∑ π, Finpartition.partitionProduct (fun T => ↑T.card.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff T.card) Z) ↑π
name: Combinatorics.replicaCoeffPolynomial_descPochhammerCoeff_eq_fixedBlockMomentSum
docString:
The falling-factorial coefficient in the power-series replica polynomial is the sum of
products of factorial-normalized moments over set partitions with the corresponding number of
blocks.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Field R] [CharZero R] {Z : PowerSeries R},
  PowerSeries.constantCoeff Z = 1 →
    ∀ (κ : Finset α → R) (s : Finset α),
      (∀ (T : Finset α), ↑T.card.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff T.card) Z = Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ T) →
        Z.replicaCoeffPolynomial s.card = Finpartition.replicaPolynomial κ s
name: Combinatorics.replicaCoeffPolynomial_eq_replicaPolynomial
docString:
Under the forward finite-set moment relation, the fixed-order power-series replica polynomial
is exactly the finite-set replica polynomial.  This is the algebraic bridge between the two replica
constructions and uses no moment-cumulant inversion.

statement: {m : ℕ} → {R : Type u_1} → [CommSemiring R] → R → Combinatorics.SideSplitting m → R
name: Combinatorics.sideSplittingWeight
docString:

is deliberately hidden; callers only need that it depends on `ζ` and the chosen side splitting.

docString: Total weight of the single-orbit permutations on a finite support set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {inst : DecidableEq α} [inst_1 : DecidableEq α] [inst_2 : Fintype α] {R : Type u_2}
  [inst_3 : CommSemiring R] (ζ ζ_1 : R),
  ζ = ζ_1 →
    ∀ (K K_1 : α → α → R),
      K = K_1 →
        ∀ (S S_1 : Finset α),
          S = S_1 → Combinatorics.singleCycleContribution ζ K S = Combinatorics.singleCycleContribution ζ_1 K_1 S_1

∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Fintype α] {R : Type u_2} [inst_2 : CommSemiring R] (ζ : R)
  (K : α → α → R) (S : Finset α),

name: Combinatorics.singleCycleContribution.eq_1

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Fintype α] {R : Type u_2} [inst_2 : CommSemiring R] (ζ : R)
  (K : α → α → R) (S : Finset α),
  Combinatorics.singleCycleContribution ζ K S = ζ ^ (S.card - 1) * Combinatorics.singleCycleContribution 1 K S

docString:
The exchange weight of a connected permutation factors universally from the
kernel-dependent contribution.

docString:
On the full finite index type, the connected contribution is the direct sum over permutations
that are a single cycle on the whole type, with the universal connected-cycle weight.

    ∑ x, Combinatorics.singleCycleContribution ζ (fun a b => K (x a) (x b)) Finset.univ =

docString:
Summing the connected single-cycle contribution over all physical-index assignments gives
`ζ^(m-1) (m-1)! tr(K^m)` for positive label count `m`. This is the public trace bridge; the raw
assignment-kernel and cycle-enumeration objects remain implementation details.

  (pairA : A → Fin (2 * n) × Fin (2 * n)) (pairB : B → Fin (2 * m) × Fin (2 * m)) (e : A ≃ B),
  (∀ (p q : A), Combinatorics.Crosses (pairA p) (pairA q) ↔ Combinatorics.Crosses (pairB (e p)) (pairB (e q))) →
    (∑ p, ∑ q, if Combinatorics.Crosses (pairA p) (pairA q) then 1 else 0) =
      ∑ p, ∑ q, if Combinatorics.Crosses (pairB p) (pairB q) then 1 else 0

docString: A crossing-preserving equivalence of finite pair families preserves the double crossing count.

Shift an arbitrary differential functional from the source into the current without changing
what the balance law says.

For `K : OneForm' → Obs'`, this realizes

```text

S' = S - K ∘ d.
```

The subtraction is written as scalar multiplication by `-1`, so the construction only needs the
module structure on observables.

    (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt test (testDerivative x) x) →
      (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt current (currentDerivative x) x) →
        IntervalIntegrable testDerivative MeasureTheory.volume a b →
          IntervalIntegrable currentDerivative MeasureTheory.volume a b →
            ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, test x * densityTimeDerivative x =
              (∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, testDerivative x * current x) - (test b * current b - test a * current a)

name: ContinuousLinearMap.HasSummableRealEigenvalues
docString:
The absolute values of the indexed nonzero real eigenvalues of `T`, with multiplicity, are
summable.

For the compact self-adjoint operators used by this project, this is the spectral summability
condition underlying spectral-trace arguments. The predicate itself deliberately does **not** assert
compactness or symmetry; those hypotheses are supplied separately wherever the spectral theorem is
used.

No separate "independent of the choice of eigenbasis" lemma is needed here: `EigenvectorIndex T`
and the eigenvalue recorded at each index (`a.1.1`) depend only on the eigenspaces of `T` and their
dimensions, not on which orthonormal basis `stdOrthonormalBasis` happens to pick within each
(possibly multi-dimensional) eigenspace.

**The kernel and `eigenvectorFamily`'s span together are dense.** Their (algebraic) sum
equals the sum of *all* eigenspaces of `T` (over `ℂ`), which is dense by
`orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_eq_bot` — since a self-adjoint operator's eigenvalues are
always real, no eigenspace outside `ℝ` (hence outside the kernel-or-nonzero-real split) is ever
missed. The second of the two structural facts combined by
`orthogonal_closure_span_eigenvectorFamily`.

orthogonal complements.** The key structural fact enabling the `tsum` reconstruction of `T`,
combining `span_eigenvectorFamily_le_kernel_orthogonal` (mutual orthogonality) with
`kernel_sup_span_eigenvectorFamily_dense` (density of their sum).

The (algebraic) span of `eigenvectorFamily` is exactly the sum of all the nonzero
eigenspaces: each per-eigenspace `stdOrthonormalBasis` spans its own (finite-dimensional)
eigenspace, and these are glued together in the same way as the index type.

**`eigenvectorFamily`'s span lies inside the orthogonal complement of the kernel.** Each
eigenvector `eigenvectorFamily hT a` lies in a *nonzero*-eigenvalue eigenspace, which is
orthogonal to the eigenvalue-`0` eigenspace `ker T` (`IsSymmetric.orthogonalFamily_eigenspaces`),
so their span is too. The first of the two structural facts combined by
`orthogonal_closure_span_eigenvectorFamily`.

    (Summable fun j => ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T) (f j)‖ ^ 2) ∧

name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_norm_sq_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq
docString:
**The core basis-independence computation.** If `T` is Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to a
basis `d`, then its adjoint `T†` is Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to *any* basis `f`, with the same
sum of squared norms. This is what makes `IsHilbertSchmidtWrt` (and, applying this twice via
`T†† = T`, comparisons between *any* two bases for `T` itself) basis-independent.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {ι : Type u_2}
  {κ : Type u_3} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (f : HilbertBasis κ ℂ H) (T : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (Summable fun i => ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2) →
    (Summable fun j => ‖T (f j)‖ ^ 2) ∧ ∑' (j : κ), ‖T (f j)‖ ^ 2 = ∑' (i : ι), ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_norm_sq_apply_and_tsum_eq
docString:
**The same basis-independence, phrased for `T` itself rather than its adjoint.** Applying
`summable_norm_sq_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq` twice — once for `T`, once for `T†` — and using
`T†† = T` transports the sum of squared norms of `T` from any one basis to any other. This
value-level result underlies the canonical basis-independent characterization below.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {S : H →L[ℂ] H},
  (Summable fun a => ↑a.fst) →
    ∑' (a : S.EigenvectorIndex), ↑a.fst =
      ∑' (μ : { ν // ν ≠ 0 }), ↑(Module.finrank ℂ ↥(Module.End.eigenspace ↑S ↑↑μ)) * ↑μ

docString:
Splits the spectral-trace `tsum` over `EigenvectorIndex S` into an outer sum over the
base nonzero eigenvalues and an inner finite sum over each eigenspace's basis vectors.

∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ) (σ : ℝ),
  Dyson.integrand V lam n σ = lam • (V σ * Dyson.term V lam σ n)
name: Dyson.integrand.eq_1

statement: ℝ → ℝ → ℂ → ℕ → ℝ
name: Dyson.integrandMajorant
docString: A constant-in-time summable majorant for the Volterra integrand on `[0, β]`.

statement: ∀ (M β : ℝ) (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ), Dyson.integrandMajorant M β lam n = ‖lam‖ * M * Dyson.majorant (‖lam‖ * M) β n
name: Dyson.integrandMajorant.eq_1

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (τ : ℝ) (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ),
  ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, Dyson.integrand V lam n σ = -Dyson.term V lam τ (n + 1)
name: Dyson.intervalIntegral_integrand
docString: Integrating the `n`th generic Volterra term gives the negative `(n+1)`st Dyson term.

statement: ℝ → ℝ → ℕ → ℝ
name: Dyson.majorant
docString: The scalar exponential-series majorant `(M τ)ⁿ / n!`.

statement: ∀ (M τ : ℝ) (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant M τ n = (↑n.factorial)⁻¹ * (M * τ) ^ n
name: Dyson.majorant.eq_1

statement: ∀ {M τ β : ℝ}, 0 ≤ M → 0 ≤ τ → τ ≤ β → ∀ (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant M τ n ≤ Dyson.majorant M β n
name: Dyson.majorant_mono_time
docString: The factorial majorant is monotone in nonnegative time.

statement: ∀ {M τ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ M → 0 ≤ τ → ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 ≤ Dyson.majorant M τ n
name: Dyson.majorant_nonneg
docString: The Dyson majorant is nonnegative for nonnegative `M` and `τ`.

statement:
∀ {r M τ : ℝ},
  0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ M → 0 ≤ τ → ∀ (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant (r * M) τ (n + 2) ≤ r ^ 2 * Dyson.majorant M τ (n + 2)
name: Dyson.majorant_norm_mul_le_sq_mul_majorant
docString:
On the unit coupling ball, each shifted majorant term factors out two powers of the coupling
norm.

statement: ∀ (M τ : ℝ), Dyson.majorant M τ 0 = 1
name: Dyson.majorant_zero

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CStarAlgebra A] {V : ℝ → A},
  (∀ (s : ℝ), star (V s) = V s) →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ),
      star lam = -lam →
        ∀ {β M t : ℝ},
          0 ≤ β →
            Dyson.ContinuousBoundedInteraction V β M →
              t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → Dyson.evolution V lam t * star (Dyson.evolution V lam t) = 1
name: Dyson.mul_star_evolution_eq_one_of_star_eq
docString:
A Dyson evolution with self-adjoint interaction and skew-adjoint scalar coupling satisfies
`U(t) U(t)† = 1`.

statement: ∀ {G : Type u_3} [inst : AddGroup G] {a b : G}, (a - b = 0) = (a = b)

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M : ℝ},

docString:
The canonical bounded-interaction hypotheses imply the standard factorial estimate for all
generic Dyson coefficients on `[0, β]`.

statement:

  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ) {τ : ℝ},
      τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
        ‖Dyson.evolution V lam τ - (1 + Dyson.term V lam τ 1)‖ ≤ ∑' (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant (‖lam‖ * M) τ (n + 2)
name: Dyson.norm_evolution_sub_one_add_term_one_le_of_bound
docString:
The part of the bounded Dyson evolution beyond first order is controlled by the corresponding
shifted factorial-majorant series.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M : ℝ},
  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ),

        ∀ {τ : ℝ},
          τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →

docString:
On the unit coupling ball, the complete Dyson remainder beyond first order is quadratic in the
coupling norm, with an explicit coupling-independent factorial tail.

statement:

docString: Uniform pointwise norm control of every generic Volterra-integrand term on `[0, β]`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] {V : ℝ → A} {β M : ℝ},
  Dyson.BoundedInteraction V β M →

docString:
The weighted `n`th coefficient is controlled by the factorial majorant with interaction bound
`‖λ‖ M`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CStarAlgebra A] {V : ℝ → A},
  (∀ (s : ℝ), star (V s) = V s) →

A Dyson evolution with self-adjoint interaction and skew-adjoint scalar coupling satisfies

docString: The weighted generic Dyson coefficients are summable at each time in a bounded interval.

statement: {A : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedRing A] → [NormedAlgebra ℂ A] → (ℝ → A) → ℂ → ℝ → ℕ → A
name: Dyson.term
docString: The `n`th perturbatively weighted Dyson coefficient.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ) (n : ℕ),
  Dyson.term V lam τ n = lam ^ n • Dyson.coeff V n τ

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ),
  Dyson.term V lam 0 n = if n = 0 then 1 else 0
name: Dyson.term_at_zero
docString: At the initial time, all positive-order weighted coefficients vanish.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  Dyson.term V lam τ 1 = -lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, V σ

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ),

name: Dyson.term_zero

name: Finpartition.PartOrdersCompatible

A family of part-local orders is compatible with a global order when every part appears in the
ambient slots in precisely that local order.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s)
  (orders : π.PartOrders),

name: Finpartition.PartShuffle

statement:
{α : Type u_1} →

name: Finpartition.assembleOrder
docString: Assemble a global order from part-local orders and an order-preserving shuffle.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (orders : π.PartOrders)
  (shuffle : π.PartShuffle),
  π.assembleOrder orders shuffle =
    Combinatorics.assembleFamilyOrderOfSize (fun B => ↥↑B) (fun B => (↑B).card) π.equivSigmaParts orders shuffle

  (orders : π.PartOrders) (h : π.PartOrdersCompatible order orders),
  π.assembleOrder orders (π.shuffleOfOrder order orders h) = order
name: Finpartition.assembleOrder_shuffleOfOrder
docString:
Reassembling a global order from compatible part-local orders and its extracted shuffle is the
original global order.

The replica-count polynomial associated with finite-set block weights.

Each partition contributes its block-product weight in degree equal to its number of blocks.

name: Finpartition.replicaPolynomial_coeff_one

For nonempty support, the coefficient linear in the replica count is exactly the one-block
contribution.

  Finpartition.replicaPolynomial κ S =

      Polynomial.C (∑ π, ↑(π.parts.card.stirlingSecond k) * Finpartition.partitionProduct κ π) * descPochhammer F k
name: Finpartition.replicaPolynomial_eq_sum_descPochhammer_stirling
docString:
The replica polynomial in the descending-factorial basis, grouped by the number of outer
blocks.  The coefficient of the `k`-th descending factorial is the Stirling-weighted sum over all
fine partitions.

statement: ∀ {n m : ℕ}, (m ∈ Finset.range n) = (m < n)

The replica polynomial in the descending-factorial basis.  The Stirling number of the second

docString:
Evaluating the replica polynomial at a natural replica number is the sum over independent
replica labelings of the blocks of every partition. Each labeling carries the partition's block
weight.

docString:
The Fredholm determinant attached to explicit diagonal coefficients `coeff`.

The definition is total, as is Mathlib's `tprod`; analytic theorems below state the absolute
summability hypothesis that guarantees convergence.

name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_eq_det_one_add_diagonalOp

On a finite Hilbert basis, the diagonal Fredholm determinant agrees with Mathlib's ordinary
determinant of `1 + diagonalOp b coeff`.

that finite product.

For absolutely summable diagonal data, the determinant vanishes exactly when one coefficient is
`-1`, equivalently when one factor `1 + coeff i` vanishes.

name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_fintype
docString:
On a finite index type, the diagonal Fredholm determinant is the ordinary finite product of the
diagonal factors.

docString: If no diagonal factor vanishes, the absolutely convergent determinant is nonzero.

No topology is imposed on `V`. Instead, every algebraic complex-linear functional `V →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ`

derivative.

Reparametrizing an algebraic-vector-valued family by a scalar differentiable map obeys the
chain rule.

  ℏ ≠ 0 →
    ∀ {s : Set ℝ} {bound : ℝ → ℝ} (ψ : ℝ → SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) {ψt : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ} {potential : ℝ → ℝ},
      s ∈ nhds t →
        (∀ τ ∈ s,
            MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
              (fun x => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityValue ((ψ τ) x))
              MeasureTheory.volume) →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable
              (fun x => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityValue ((ψ t) x))
              MeasureTheory.volume →
            MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
                (fun x =>
                  QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityTimeDerivativeValue ((ψ t) x) (ψt t x))
                MeasureTheory.volume →
              (∀ (x τ : ℝ),
                  τ ∈ s →
                    ‖QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityTimeDerivativeValue ((ψ τ) x)
                          (ψt τ x)‖ ≤
                      bound x) →
                MeasureTheory.Integrable bound MeasureTheory.volume →
                  (∀ (x τ : ℝ), τ ∈ s → HasDerivAt (fun u => ((ψ u) x).re) (ψt τ x).re τ) →
                    (∀ (x τ : ℝ), τ ∈ s → HasDerivAt (fun u => ((ψ u) x).im) (ψt τ x).im τ) →
                      (∀ (x : ℝ),
                          Complex.I * ↑ℏ * ψt t x =
                            -↑κ *
                                (QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.schwartzSpatialSecondDerivative1D (ψ t)) x +
                              ↑(potential x) * (ψ t) x) →
                        deriv (fun τ => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.totalProbability1D ⇑(ψ τ)) t = 0

`d/dt ∫ test * ρ = ∫ (deriv test) * j`.

The support condition is stated as `tsupport test ⊆ Ioo a b`, making the compact support window and
the disappearance of the boundary current explicit at the theorem boundary.

docString:
Finite-observation-time adiabatic response of a neutral response channel.

The source value at the observation time has been factored out, so the retarded kernel carries the
lag phase `exp ((i ω - η) (T - s))` while the explicit observable variation contributes its
contact expectation at `T`. No stationarity or infinite-time limit is assumed.

  channel.finiteTimeAdiabaticResponse system expectation ω η T =
    (∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..T,
        QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticFrequencyPhase ω η (T - s) *
          channel.retardedKernel system expectation T s) +
      channel.contactExpectation system expectation T

  (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H) (V : ℝ → H →L[ℂ] H) (lam t : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentPerturbedObservableMap system V lam t =
    (ContinuousLinearMap.mul ℂ (H →L[ℂ] H)).flip
        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.freePropagator system t *

          QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.freePropagator system (-t))

name: QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.BandEdgeData
docString:
Local data for a nondegenerate finite-model band edge.

The edge lies in the finite energy and Bloch-coordinate domains, and the local branch satisfies
the Bloch dispersion relation on a neighborhood of the edge. Local differentiability assumptions
are explicit; the curvature identity itself is not a field and is derived below by differentiating
the Bloch relation twice.

statement:
{params : QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.Parameters} →
  {motive : QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.BandEdgeData params → Sort u} →
    (t : QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.BandEdgeData params) →
      ((branchEnergy : ℝ → ℝ) →
          (blochCoordinate energy curvature discriminantSlope : ℝ) →
            (energy_eq : branchEnergy blochCoordinate = energy) →
              (energy_mem : QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.inEnergyDomain params energy) →
                (bloch_mem : QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.inBlochDomain params blochCoordinate) →
                  (bloch_relation :
                      (fun k =>
                          QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant params
                            (branchEnergy k)) =ᶠ[nhds blochCoordinate]
                        fun k => Real.cos (k * params.period)) →
                    (branchDifferentiable : ∀ᶠ (k : ℝ) in nhds blochCoordinate, DifferentiableAt ℝ branchEnergy k) →
                      (discriminantDifferentiable :
                          ∀ᶠ (k : ℝ) in nhds blochCoordinate,
                            DifferentiableAt ℝ (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant params)
                              (branchEnergy k)) →
                        (stationary : HasDerivAt branchEnergy 0 blochCoordinate) →
                          (secondDerivative : HasDerivAt (fun k => deriv branchEnergy k) curvature blochCoordinate) →
                            (discriminantDerivative :
                                HasDerivAt (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant params) discriminantSlope
                                  energy) →
                              (discriminantDerivativeDifferentiable :
                                  DifferentiableAt ℝ
                                    (fun e => deriv (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant params) e) energy) →
                                (discriminantSlope_ne_zero : discriminantSlope ≠ 0) →
                                  (phaseCurvatureDenominator_ne_zero :
                                      params.period ^ 2 * Real.cos (blochCoordinate * params.period) ≠ 0) →
                                    motive
                                      { branchEnergy := branchEnergy, blochCoordinate := blochCoordinate,
                                        energy := energy, curvature := curvature,
                                        discriminantSlope := discriminantSlope, energy_eq := energy_eq,
                                        energy_mem := energy_mem, bloch_mem := bloch_mem,
                                        bloch_relation := bloch_relation, branchDifferentiable := branchDifferentiable,
                                        discriminantDifferentiable := discriminantDifferentiable,
                                        stationary := stationary, secondDerivative := secondDerivative,
                                        discriminantDerivative := discriminantDerivative,
                                        discriminantDerivativeDifferentiable := discriminantDerivativeDifferentiable,
                                        discriminantSlope_ne_zero := discriminantSlope_ne_zero,
                                        phaseCurvatureDenominator_ne_zero := phaseCurvatureDenominator_ne_zero }) →
        motive t

    ↑(2 * Real.cos (k * params.period))

statement: QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.Parameters → ℝ → ℝ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant
docString:
Kronig–Penney discriminant with the normalization exposed explicitly as
`Δ(E) = tr M(E) / 2`.

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.Parameters) (energy : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant params energy =
    (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.oneCellTransfer params energy).trace / 2
name: QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant.eq_1

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.Parameters),
  params.IsRegular →
    ∀ {energy : ℝ},
      QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.inEnergyDomain params energy →
        QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant params energy =
          Real.cos (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy * params.barrierWidth) *
              Real.cos (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy * params.wellWidth) -
            (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy /
                      QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy +
                    QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy /
                      QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy) /
                  2 *
                Real.sin (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.barrierWaveNumber params energy * params.barrierWidth) *
              Real.sin (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.wellWaveNumber params energy * params.wellWidth)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.discriminant_eq_closedForm
docString:
Closed form of the one-cell Kronig–Penney discriminant on the regular finite energy domain.
Both local wave numbers are nonzero there, so this is the standard physical transfer-matrix
dispersion formula rather than an artifact of totalized division.

statement: ℝ → ℝ → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.regionTransfer
docString:
Transfer matrix through a constant-potential region of width `width` with nonzero real wave
number `q`, acting on `(ψ, ∂ₓψ)`. The totalized formula is defined for every `q`; determinant
statements below state the required nonzero hypothesis explicitly.

statement:
∀ (q width : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.regionTransfer q width =
    !![Real.cos (q * width), Real.sin (q * width) / q; -(q * Real.sin (q * width)), Real.cos (q * width)]
name: QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.regionTransfer.eq_1

statement: ∀ (q width : ℝ), q ≠ 0 → (QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.regionTransfer q width).det = 1
name: QuantumTheory.Models.KronigPenney.regionTransfer_det
docString: A constant-region transfer matrix is unimodular whenever its wave number is nonzero.

channels. Positivity requires the physical hypotheses proved downstream when needed.

statement: QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℂ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveEnergy
docString: Side-indexed effective energy after retaining the metallic Born scalar damping channel.

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveEnergy side v probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar =
    ↑probeEnergy +
      ↑(side.sign * QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDampingScale v disorderStrength hbar * probeEnergy) *
        Complex.I
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveEnergy.eq_1

statement: QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℂ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveMass
docString: Side-indexed effective Dirac mass after retaining the metallic Born `σ_z` damping channel.

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveMass side v m disorderStrength hbar =
    ↑m -
      ↑(side.sign * QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDampingScale v disorderStrength hbar * m) * Complex.I
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveMass.eq_1

statement: QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℂ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator
docString: Quadratic denominator of the Born-dressed two-band propagator.

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator side v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength
      hbar =
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveEnergy side v probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar ^ 2 -
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveMass side v m disorderStrength hbar ^ 2 -
      ↑(v ^ 2 * (px ^ 2 + py ^ 2))
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator.eq_1

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator side v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength
      hbar =
    ↑((1 - QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDampingScale v disorderStrength hbar ^ 2) *
            (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) -
          v ^ 2 * (px ^ 2 + py ^ 2)) +
      ↑(2 * side.sign * QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDampingScale v disorderStrength hbar *
            (probeEnergy ^ 2 + m ^ 2)) *
        Complex.I
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator_eq_closedForm
docString:
Closed side-indexed form of the Born-dressed denominator used by the radial retarded-advanced
rung. Its real part is even in the spectral side, while its imaginary part changes sign.

statement:
∀ (v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m
        p 0 probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar *
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced
        v m p 0 probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar =
    ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorProduct v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator_retarded_mul_advanced_radial_eq
docString: The radial Cartesian Born denominators multiply to the canonical real weak-Born RA product.

statement: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.PauliAxis → QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℂ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenPauliCoefficient
docString: Direction-indexed Pauli-vector coefficient of the Born-dressed propagator.

statement:
∀ (axis : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.PauliAxis) (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide)
  (v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenPauliCoefficient axis side v m px py probeEnergy
      disorderStrength hbar =
    (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator side v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength
          hbar)⁻¹ *
      InternalSpace.pauliAxisComponent axis (↑(v * px)) (↑(v * py))
        (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveMass side v m disorderStrength hbar)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenPauliCoefficient.eq_1

statement: QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℂ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenScalarCoefficient
docString: Identity coefficient of the Born-dressed Pauli propagator.

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenScalarCoefficient side v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength
      hbar =
    (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenDenominator side v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength
          hbar)⁻¹ *
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornEffectiveEnergy side v probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenScalarCoefficient.eq_1

statement: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorCenter
docString: Real radial center of the weak-Born retarded-advanced denominator pair.

statement:
∀ (v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorCenter v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar =
    (1 - QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDampingScale v disorderStrength hbar ^ 2) *
        (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) -
      v ^ 2 * p ^ 2
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorCenter.eq_1

statement: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorProduct
docString: Manifestly real weak-Born retarded-advanced denominator product.

statement:
∀ (v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorProduct v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar =
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorCenter v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar ^ 2 +
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorWidth v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar ^ 2
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorProduct.eq_1

statement:
∀ (v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  0 ≤ QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorProduct v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorProduct_nonneg
docString: The real weak-Born retarded-advanced denominator product is nonnegative.

docString: Signed width parameter multiplying `i` in the weak-Born retarded denominator.

statement: (1 + 1).AtLeastTwo

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorWidth v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar =

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorWidth.eq_1

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy hbar gamma : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    hbar ≠ 0 →
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorWidth v m probeEnergy
          (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDisorderStrengthOfDampingScale v hbar gamma) hbar =
        2 * gamma * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + m ^ 2)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorWidth_weakDisorderStrength
docString: Under `W(γ) = 4 γ ℏ² v²`, the RA denominator width is `2γ(ε²+m²)`.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRadialDenominatorIntegrandOfRegulator
docString:

Jacobian `p`.

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy regulator p : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRadialDenominatorIntegrandOfRegulator v m probeEnergy regulator p =
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.massiveDiracRadialDenominatorKernel v p
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator probeEnergy regulator) ↑m
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRadialDenominatorIntegrandOfRegulator.eq_1

statement: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.DiracHilbert →L[ℂ] QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.DiracHilbert

docString:
Operator-valued radial Green kernel at an arbitrary signed regulator before continuum disorder
and measure prefactors are applied.

statement: SMulCommClass ℂ ℂ (WithLp 2 (Fin 2 → ℂ))
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRadialGreenKernelOfRegulator._proof_1

statement: ContinuousConstSMul ℂ QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.DiracHilbert
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRadialGreenKernelOfRegulator._proof_2

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy regulator p : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRadialGreenKernelOfRegulator v m probeEnergy regulator p =

statement: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.BornSelfEnergyChannel → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℂ

docString:
Radial Born integrand for either surviving isotropic self-energy channel at an arbitrary signed

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy regulator p : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRadialIntegrandOfRegulator
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.BornSelfEnergyChannel.scalar v m probeEnergy regulator p =
    ↑p * QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenScalarCoefficientOfRegulator v m p 0 probeEnergy regulator

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy regulator p : ℝ),

statement: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRetardedAdvancedCurrentRungArctanPhase
docString: Arctangent phase adapted to the real retarded-advanced denominator pair `A(p)² + B²`.

statement:
∀ (v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRetardedAdvancedCurrentRungArctanPhase v m p probeEnergy
      disorderStrength hbar =
    Real.arctan
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorCenter v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar /
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRADenominatorWidth v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRetardedAdvancedCurrentRungArctanPhase.eq_1

statement: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → Fin 2 → ℂ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRetardedAdvancedPauliXAngularCoefficient
docString:
Direction-indexed coefficient vector after the full polar-angle integral of the Born-dressed
`Gᴿ σₓ Gᴬ` rung. The transverse sign is specific to this retarded/advanced ordering.

statement:
∀ (v m p probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRetardedAdvancedPauliXAngularCoefficient v m p probeEnergy
      disorderStrength hbar =
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliRungAngularCoefficient
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenScalarCoefficient
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar)
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenScalarCoefficient
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar)
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar)
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRetardedAdvancedPauliXAngularCoefficient.eq_1

statement: (7 + 1).AtLeastTwo
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRetardedAdvancedPauliXAngularNumerator._proof_1

statement:
∀ (output : Fin 2) (v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornRetardedAdvancedPauliXAngularNumerator output v m probeEnergy
      disorderStrength hbar =
    ![2 * Real.pi * (1 + QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDampingScale v disorderStrength hbar ^ 2) *
          (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2),
        8 * Real.pi * QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDampingScale v disorderStrength hbar *
            probeEnergy *
          m]
      output

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  hbar ≠ 0 →

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteBroadeningSameSideRadialEndpoint side v m probeEnergy broadening
      disorderStrength hbar pMax =
    (↑(2 * v ^ 2))⁻¹ *
        (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy side v m probeEnergy broadening
              disorderStrength hbar pMax ^
            2 -
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass side v m probeEnergy broadening
              disorderStrength hbar pMax ^
            2) *
      ((QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator side v m pMax 0 probeEnergy
            broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)⁻¹ -
        (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator side v m 0 0 probeEnergy broadening
            disorderStrength hbar pMax)⁻¹)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteBroadeningSameSideRadialEndpoint.eq_1

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    broadening ≠ 0 →
      0 ≤ disorderStrength →
        0 ≤ pMax →
          IntervalIntegrable
              (fun p =>
                ↑p *
                    (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator side v m p 0
                          probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)⁻¹ ^
                      2 *
                  (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy side v m probeEnergy
                        broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax ^
                      2 -
                    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass side v m probeEnergy
                        broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax ^
                      2))
              MeasureTheory.volume 0 pMax ∧
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                ↑p *
                    (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator side v m p 0
                          probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)⁻¹ ^
                      2 *
                  (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy side v m probeEnergy
                        broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax ^
                      2 -
                    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass side v m probeEnergy
                        broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax ^
                      2) =
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteBroadeningSameSideRadialEndpoint side v m probeEnergy broadening
                disorderStrength hbar pMax

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegralBoundaryValue
docString:
Complex finite-cutoff metallic boundary value of the common Born denominator integral. The
imaginary component retains the retarded/advanced side through `side.sign`; it is intentionally not
written as the principal logarithm evaluated directly on the negative real axis, where the side of
approach would be lost.

statement: (1 + 1).AtLeastTwo

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m probeEnergy pMax : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegralBoundaryValue side v m probeEnergy
      pMax =
    {
      re :=
        -(2 * v ^ 2)⁻¹ *
          (Real.log ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenDenominator side v m pMax 0 probeEnergy 0‖ -
            Real.log ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenDenominator side v m 0 0 probeEnergy 0‖),
      im := -(2 * v ^ 2)⁻¹ * (side.sign * Real.pi) }

statement:

        pMax).im =
    -(2 * v ^ 2)⁻¹ * (side.sign * Real.pi)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegralBoundaryValue_im

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m probeEnergy pMax : ℝ),

        pMax).re =

        Real.log ‖QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenDenominator side v m 0 0 probeEnergy 0‖)

        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegralBoundaryValue

docString:

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegralOfRegulator
docString:

signed regulator.

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy regulator pMax : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    probeEnergy ≠ 0 →
      regulator ≠ 0 →
        (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegralOfRegulator v m probeEnergy
              regulator pMax).re =
          -(2 * v ^ 2)⁻¹ *
            (Real.log
                √((probeEnergy ^ 2 - regulator ^ 2 - m ^ 2 - v ^ 2 * pMax ^ 2) ^ 2 +
                    (2 * probeEnergy * regulator) ^ 2) -
              Real.log √((probeEnergy ^ 2 - regulator ^ 2 - m ^ 2) ^ 2 + (2 * probeEnergy * regulator) ^ 2))

polynomial.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegral_im_eq

statement:

  v ≠ 0 →
    probeEnergy ≠ 0 →
      broadening ≠ 0 →
        (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegral side v m probeEnergy broadening

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialTraceKernel
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.psi v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax
      radius =
    have a :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentScalarCoefficient 0 v
        m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have b :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenScalarCoefficient
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have c := b;
    have d :=
      -QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentScalarCoefficient 1 v
          m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have ux :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x 0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have uy :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y 0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have uz :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z 0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have qx :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x 1 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have qy :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y 1 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have qz :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonGaussianCrossedRadialCurrentPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z 1 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have grx :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening
        disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have grz :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenPauliCoefficient
        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening
        disorderStrength hbar pMax radius;
    have amplitude :=
      2 *
        ((a * b - ux * grx + uz * grz) * (c * d + grx * qx - grz * qz) +
              (-a * grx + b * ux + Complex.I * uy * grz) * (c * qx + d * grx - Complex.I * grz * qy) +
            (b * uy - Complex.I * (uz * grx + ux * grz)) * (c * qy + Complex.I * (grz * qx + grx * qz)) +
          (a * grz + b * uz + Complex.I * uy * grx) * (-c * qz + d * grz + Complex.I * grx * qy));
    amplitude + (starRingEnd ℂ) amplitude

statement:
∀ (axis : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.PauliAxis) (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide)
  (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenPauliCoefficient axis side v m probeEnergy
      broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius =
    match axis with
    | InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x =>
      ((↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel side v m
                probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius p 0 1) +
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel side v m
                probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius p 1 0) /
        2
    | InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y =>
      Complex.I *
          ((↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel side v m
                  probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius p 0 1) -
            ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
              ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel side v m
                  probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius p 1 0) /
        2
    | InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z =>
      ((↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel side v m
                probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius p 0 0) -
          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
            ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialGreenEntryKernel side v m
                probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius p 1 1) /
        2

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialRealSpaceGreenMatrix
docString:
One-dimensional radial-kernel representation of the finite-cutoff Born-Dyson Green matrix on
the positive real-space radial axis. The diagonal channels carry the zeroth angular kernel, while
the off-diagonal in-plane channel carries the first-cosine kernel.

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialRealSpaceGreenMatrix side v m probeEnergy
      broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax radius =
    !![↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
          ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
            ↑p *
              ((fun p => QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) p *
                ((fun p =>
                      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient side v m p 0
                        probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)
                    p +
                  (fun p =>
                      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)
                    p)),
        ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
          ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
            ↑p *
              ((fun p => QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) p *
                (fun p =>
                    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                      InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)
                  p);
      ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
          ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
            ↑p *
              ((fun p => QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) p *
                (fun p =>
                    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                      InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)
                  p),
        ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
          ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
            ↑p *
              ((fun p => QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar)) p *
                ((fun p =>
                      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonScalarCoefficient side v m p 0
                        probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)
                    p -
                  (fun p =>
                      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonPauliCoefficient
                        InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z side v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)
                    p))]
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRadialRealSpaceGreenMatrix.eq_1

statement:

  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRetardedAdvancedAngularNumerator i j v m probeEnergy
      broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax =
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneRotationMatrix
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneCoefficientVector
        (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
              QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax *
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
              QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax -
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
              QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax *
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
              QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax)
        (Complex.I *
          (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
                QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax *
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
                QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax -
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
                QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax *

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRetardedAdvancedDressedSurfaceAngularTraceRadialCoefficient
docString:
Explicit pair-indexed radial coefficient of the finite-`η` RA-dressed Středa angular trace. The
RA and same-side rungs act on complete dressed and bare in-plane source vectors; the requested
measured-current direction is the final projection.

statement: (1 + 1).AtLeastTwo

statement:
∀ (e v m p probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRetardedAdvancedDressedSurfaceAngularTraceRadialCoefficient
      0 0 e v m p probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax =
    have q := ↑(-e) * ↑v;
    have solved :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonRetardedAdvancedDressedSourceCurrentCoefficientVector
        0 v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have eR :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have massR :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have dR :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have eA :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveEnergy
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have massA :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornEffectiveMass
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    have dA :=
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonDenominator
        QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced v m p 0 probeEnergy broadening disorderStrength hbar pMax;
    ↑(4 * Real.pi) * q ^ 2 *
      (dR⁻¹ * dA⁻¹ * ((eR * eA - massR * massA) * solved 0 - Complex.I * (eA * massR - eR * massA) * solved 1) -
        1 / 2 * (dR⁻¹ ^ 2 * (eR ^ 2 - massR ^ 2) + dA⁻¹ ^ 2 * (eA ^ 2 - massA ^ 2)))

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.gaussianCrossedTraceKernel
docString:
Pointwise trace kernel for the two leading crossed Gaussian Hall topologies.

The separation type is required only to support `r ↦ -r`, allowing the same topology to be reused
for Cartesian real-space vectors and scalar radial coordinates.

The `realSpaceCurrentBlock` argument is Ado's `J_r` block from Eq. (14), not the local dressed vertex
`Γ`. For `x` this is
`Tr(Jˣ(r) Gᴿ(-r) Jʸ(r) Gᴬ(-r))`.

For `psi` the traced amplitude is
`Tr(Jˣ(r) Gᴿ(-r) Gᴿ(r) Jʸ(-r)) + h.c.`;
the Hermitian-conjugate contribution is represented after taking the trace as complex conjugation.

statement: NeZero (1 + 1)

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Neg R] (greenRetarded greenAdvanced : R → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2)
  (realSpaceCurrentBlock : Fin 2 → R → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2) (r : R),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.gaussianCrossedTraceKernel
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.x greenRetarded greenAdvanced realSpaceCurrentBlock r =
    (realSpaceCurrentBlock 0 r * greenRetarded (-r) * realSpaceCurrentBlock 1 r * greenAdvanced (-r)).trace
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.gaussianCrossedTraceKernel.eq_1

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Neg R] (greenRetarded greenAdvanced : R → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2)

      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.GaussianCrossedDiagram.psi greenRetarded greenAdvanced realSpaceCurrentBlock r =
    (realSpaceCurrentBlock 0 r * greenRetarded (-r) * greenRetarded r * realSpaceCurrentBlock 1 (-r)).trace +
      (starRingEnd ℂ)
        (realSpaceCurrentBlock 0 r * greenRetarded (-r) * greenRetarded r * realSpaceCurrentBlock 1 (-r)).trace

[doi:10.1209/0295-5075/111/37004](https://doi.org/10.1209/0295-5075/111/37004).
The paper's Eqs. (12a-c) are the intrinsic, side-jump, and non-crossing-skew components; the
theorem below only formalizes the ordered finite-cutoff provenance partition.
The side-jump-type term is shared between the two provenance components rather than attached to only
one of them. The `sideJumpType` and `gaussianSkewType` names are local to this theorem statement and
do not create primitive mechanism APIs.

statement: NeZero (1 + 1)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.polarPauliInPlaneHarmonics._proof_1

statement:
∀ (aL bL dL aR bR dR : ℂ) (coefficients : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.InPlaneCoefficientVector),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.polarPauliInPlaneHarmonics aL bL dL aR bR dR coefficients =
    {
      constant :=
        ((aL * aR - dL * dR) * coefficients 0 - Complex.I * (aR * dL - aL * dR) * coefficients 1) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaX +
          (Complex.I * (aR * dL - aL * dR) * coefficients 0 + (aL * aR - dL * dR) * coefficients 1) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaY,
      firstCosine :=
        ((aR * bL + aL * bR) * coefficients 0 - Complex.I * (bR * dL - bL * dR) * coefficients 1) • 1 +
          ((bR * dL + bL * dR) * coefficients 0 - Complex.I * (aL * bR - aR * bL) * coefficients 1) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaZ,
      firstSine :=
        (Complex.I * (bR * dL - bL * dR) * coefficients 0 + (aR * bL + aL * bR) * coefficients 1) • 1 +
          (Complex.I * (aL * bR - aR * bL) * coefficients 0 + (bR * dL + bL * dR) * coefficients 1) •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaZ,
      secondCosine :=
        (bL * bR * coefficients 0) • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaX -
          (bL * bR * coefficients 1) • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaY,
      secondMixed :=
        (2 * bL * bR * coefficients 1) • QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaX +

docString:
At fixed cutoff beyond the metallic shell, the canonical zero-broadening solved ladder vector
converges to the longitudinal dressed-current factor
`2 (ε² + m²) / (ε² + 3 m²)` with vanishing raw transverse component. This is the repository-oriented
weak-disorder realization of the diagonal factor `F` in Ado et al., EPL 111, 37004 (2015), Eq. (11).

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy hbar pMax : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    hbar ≠ 0 →
      |m| < probeEnergy →
        probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2 < v ^ 2 * pMax ^ 2 →
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun disorderStrength =>
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonLadderSolvedVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary v
                  m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax 1 /
                ↑disorderStrength)
            (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
            (nhds
              ↑(4 * Real.pi * QuantumTheory.Transport.fullAngleMomentumMeasurePrefactor hbar * probeEnergy * m *
                    (probeEnergy ^ 2 + m ^ 2) /
                  (v ^ 2 * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2) ^ 2)))

docString:
The transverse component of the zero-broadening dressed-current vector carries the same first
nonvanishing weak-disorder coefficient as the transverse ladder action. In the repository
`Gᴿ Γ Gᴬ` orientation, this is the scaled transverse coefficient entering the dressed-current
structure compared with Ado et al., EPL 111, 37004 (2015), Eq. (11). The retarded/advanced-order
sign and disorder-normalization conversion to Ado's `F² B` convention remain downstream.

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.tendsto_finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonOrderedXYRetardedAdvancedDressedSurfaceMomentumIntegral_broadening_zero
docString:
At fixed positive disorder and finite cutoff, the ordered `xy` Středa momentum integral converges
to its zero-broadening boundary.

statement:
∀ (e v m probeEnergy hbar pMax : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    0 < hbar →
      |m| < probeEnergy →
        probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2 < v ^ 2 * pMax ^ 2 →
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun disorderStrength =>
              have q := ↑(-e) * ↑v;
              have pref :=
                ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDisorderMeasurePrefactor disorderStrength hbar);
              have solved :=
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonLadderSolvedVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary
                  v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax;
              have rung :=
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonCurrentRungVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary
                  v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax;
              have normalization :=
                ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.bastinStredaPhysicalMomentumConductivityNormalization hbar);
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneCoefficientVector
                (normalization * (-2 * q ^ 2 * pref⁻¹ * (rung 1 * solved 0)))
                (normalization * (-2 * q ^ 2 * pref⁻¹ * (rung 0 * solved 1))))
            (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
            (nhds
              (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneCoefficientVector
                ↑(-e ^ 2 * probeEnergy * m / (Real.pi * hbar * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2)))
                ↑(-e ^ 2 * probeEnergy * m * (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) /
                    (Real.pi * hbar * (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2) ^ 2))))

  v ≠ 0 →
    hbar ≠ 0 →

        probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2 < v ^ 2 * pMax ^ 2 →
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun disorderStrength =>
              have q := ↑(-e) * ↑v;
              have pref :=
                ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornDisorderMeasurePrefactor disorderStrength hbar);
              have solved :=
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonLadderSolvedVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary
                  v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax;
              have rung :=
                QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDysonCurrentRungVectorZeroBroadeningBoundary
                  v m probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar pMax;
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneCoefficientVector (-2 * q ^ 2 * pref⁻¹ * (rung 1 * solved 0))
                (-2 * q ^ 2 * pref⁻¹ * (rung 0 * solved 1)))
            (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
            (nhds
              (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.inPlaneCoefficientVector
                ↑(-8 * Real.pi ^ 2 * e ^ 2 * probeEnergy * m / (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2))
                ↑(-8 * Real.pi ^ 2 * e ^ 2 * probeEnergy * m * (probeEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) /
                    (probeEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2) ^ 2)))
