name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedBerryWeightCutoff
docString:
Canonical zero-temperature occupied-state Berry weight at finite positive-energy cutoff. Both
bands are integrated over the same cutoff interval; the generic spectral occupation selects the
filled lower band and the occupied part of the upper band.

statement:
∀ (m fermiEnergy Λ : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedBerryWeightCutoff m fermiEnergy Λ =
    ∑ band, QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedBandBerryWeightCutoff band m fermiEnergy Λ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedBerryWeightCutoff.eq_1

statement:
∀ (m εF Λ : ℝ),
  |m| ≤ εF →
    εF ≤ Λ →
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedBerryWeightCutoff m εF Λ = m / (2 * εF) - m / (2 * Λ)
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedBerryWeightCutoff_eq
docString:
The canonical occupation-derived finite-cutoff response keeps the single-cone regulator term
explicit, including the massless endpoint where both sides vanish.

statement: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedCleanInterbandBastinPairBandCutoff
docString:

statement:

docString:

name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedCleanInterbandBastinPairRadialEnergyDensity
docString:

occupation acts directly on the clean Bastin profile at the signed band energy.

statement: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedRadialBerryEnergyDensity
docString:
Zero-temperature occupation-weighted radial Berry density. The occupation is evaluated on the
actual signed band energy `s ε`, while `ε` itself remains the positive energy coordinate used by the
radial reduction.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (m fermiEnergy ε : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedRadialBerryEnergyDensity band m fermiEnergy ε =
    QuantumTheory.Transport.bandStateOccupation (QuantumTheory.Transport.zeroTemperatureOccupation fermiEnergy)
        (fun band ε => QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.bandSign band * ε) band ε *
      QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.radialBerryEnergyDensity band m ε
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureOccupiedRadialBerryEnergyDensity.eq_1

statement: ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → QuantumTheory.Transport.PositiveTransportLifetime → ℝ
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity
docString:
Zero-temperature Fermi-surface relaxation-time-approximation benchmark for the longitudinal
electrical conductivity.

The supplied `transportLifetime` is `τ_tr`, a positive current-relaxation time assumed uniform around
the isotropic Fermi circle, which is why it multiplies the angularly averaged `v_x²` as one scalar.
This definition does not claim that `τ_tr` follows from the clean Hamiltonian or from a self-energy
broadening.

statement:
∀ (e hbar v m fermiEnergy disorderStrength : ℝ) (hvelocity : v ≠ 0) (hhbar : 0 < hbar)
  (hdisorder : 0 < disorderStrength) (hmF : |m| < fermiEnergy),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity e hbar v m fermiEnergy
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornUpperBandPositiveTransportLifetime v m fermiEnergy
        disorderStrength hbar hvelocity hhbar hdisorder hmF) =
    e ^ 2 * hbar * v ^ 2 * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / (Real.pi * disorderStrength * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2))
name: QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity_bornTransportLifetime_eq
docString:
The zero-temperature massive-Dirac RTA benchmark evaluated on the microscopic Born transport
lifetime has the explicit `1/W` form

`σxx = e² ℏ v² (εF² - m²) / [π W (εF² + 3 m²)]`.

The positivity assumptions are exactly those used to package the microscopic lifetime as a
`PositiveTransportLifetime`; no finite clean-disorder limit is asserted.

  hbar ≠ 0 →

      |m| < fermiEnergy →

name: QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.currentProductAngularCoefficients
docString:
Canonical constant/second-harmonic representation of the product of two Cartesian current
components on a circle of radius `p`.

For equal directions the constant piece is one half of `(q p / m_eff)²`; the second-cosine
coefficient distinguishes `xx` from `yy`. For unequal directions the product is purely the mixed
second harmonic. The common current scale is obtained from `currentComponent`.

statement: (1 + 1).AtLeastTwo
name: QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.currentProductAngularCoefficients._proof_1

statement:
∀ (params : QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.Parameters) (measured source : Fin 2) (p : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.currentProductAngularCoefficients params measured source p =
    if _hEq : measured = source then
      if _hX : measured = 0 then
        { constant := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) / 2, firstCosine := 0,
          firstSine := 0, secondCosine := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) / 2,
          secondMixed := 0 }
      else
        { constant := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) / 2, firstCosine := 0,
          firstSine := 0, secondCosine := -(↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) / 2),
          secondMixed := 0 }
    else
      { constant := 0, firstCosine := 0, firstSine := 0, secondCosine := 0,
        secondMixed := ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.radialCurrentScale params p ^ 2) }
name: QuantumTheory.Models.Parabolic2DEG.currentProductAngularCoefficients.eq_1

statement:

  (band : QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.Band) (px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.forceMatrixTraceNumerator params μ ν band px py =
    (QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.bandProjector params (QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.oppositeBand band) px
              py *
            QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.velocityOperator params.toHamiltonianParameters μ px py *
          QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.bandProjector params band px py *
        QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.velocityOperator params.toHamiltonianParameters ν px py).trace

    QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.forceMatrixTraceNumerator params 0 1 band px py =
      -↑(params.rashbaVelocity ^ 4 * px * py /
              QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.spinOrbitEnergy params.toHamiltonianParameters px py ^ 2) -
        ↑(QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.bandSign band * params.exchangeSplitting * params.rashbaVelocity ^ 2 /
              QuantumTheory.Models.RashbaExchange.spinOrbitEnergy params.toHamiltonianParameters px py) *
          Complex.I

  (coefficients : QuantumTheory.Transport.AngularHarmonicCoefficients E) (θ : ℝ),
  coefficients.eval θ =
    coefficients.constant + ↑(Real.cos θ) • coefficients.firstCosine + ↑(Real.sin θ) • coefficients.firstSine +
        (↑(Real.cos θ) ^ 2 - ↑(Real.sin θ) ^ 2) • coefficients.secondCosine +

    ↑p *
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel z * coefficients.constant +
          QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel z * coefficients.firstCosine +
        QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel z * coefficients.secondCosine)

  ∫ (θ : ℝ) in 0..2 * Real.pi,
      ↑p * QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierRadialPhase z (θ - angle) * coefficients.eval θ =
    ↑p *
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel z * coefficients.constant +
          QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel z *
            (↑(Real.cos angle) * coefficients.firstCosine + ↑(Real.sin angle) * coefficients.firstSine) +
        QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel z *
          ((↑(Real.cos angle) ^ 2 - ↑(Real.sin angle) ^ 2) * coefficients.secondCosine +
            ↑(Real.cos angle) * ↑(Real.sin angle) * coefficients.secondMixed))

docString:
Finite SCBA/RA charge-vertex Ward consistency. Under the minimal charge-symmetry interface and
the same conditional ladder invertibility used by the generic resummation, the generic corrected
charge vertex `Γ_Q = (I - L_RA)⁻¹ Q` obeys

`(zᴬ - zᴿ) • (Ḡᴿ Γ_Q Ḡᴬ) = Ḡᴿ Q - Q Ḡᴬ`.

For `Q = 1`, the right-hand side is `Ḡᴿ - Ḡᴬ`.

  freeInverse * freeGreen = 1 →
    freeGreen * freeInverse = 1 →
      dressedInverse * dressedGreen = 1 →
        dressedGreen * dressedInverse = 1 →
          (QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy ↔
            selfEnergy = freeInverse - dressedInverse)

definition of self-energy.

    dressedGreen = freeGreen + freeGreen * selfEnergy * dressedGreen
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.leftDyson
docString: The left-oriented Dyson equation carried by an abstract self-energy relation.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy freeShift dressedShift : A},
  freeGreen * freeShift = 1 →
    freeShift * freeGreen = 1 →

        dressedGreen * dressedShift = 1 →
          freeShift = dressedShift + selfEnergy → QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy

together with `freeShift = dressedShift + selfEnergy`.

docString: The right-oriented Dyson equation carried by an abstract self-energy relation.

docString:

  (occupation occupationDerivative surfacePrimitive surfacePrimitiveDerivative seaKernel : ℝ → ℂ)
  (occupation_continuous : ContinuousOn occupation (Set.uIcc lowerEnergy upperEnergy))
  (surfacePrimitive_continuous : ContinuousOn surfacePrimitive (Set.uIcc lowerEnergy upperEnergy))
  (occupation_hasDerivAt :
    ∀ energy ∈ Set.Ioo (min lowerEnergy upperEnergy) (max lowerEnergy upperEnergy),
      HasDerivAt occupation (occupationDerivative energy) energy)
  (surfacePrimitive_hasDerivAt :
    ∀ energy ∈ Set.Ioo (min lowerEnergy upperEnergy) (max lowerEnergy upperEnergy),
      HasDerivAt surfacePrimitive (surfacePrimitiveDerivative energy) energy)
  (occupationDerivative_intervalIntegrable :
    IntervalIntegrable occupationDerivative MeasureTheory.volume lowerEnergy upperEnergy)
  (surfacePrimitiveDerivative_intervalIntegrable :
    IntervalIntegrable surfacePrimitiveDerivative MeasureTheory.volume lowerEnergy upperEnergy)
  (seaProduct_intervalIntegrable :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun energy => occupation energy * seaKernel energy) MeasureTheory.volume lowerEnergy
      upperEnergy)
  (boundary_vanishes :
    occupation upperEnergy * surfacePrimitive upperEnergy - occupation lowerEnergy * surfacePrimitive lowerEnergy = 0),
  sizeOf
      { lowerEnergy := lowerEnergy, upperEnergy := upperEnergy, occupation := occupation,
        occupationDerivative := occupationDerivative, surfacePrimitive := surfacePrimitive,
        surfacePrimitiveDerivative := surfacePrimitiveDerivative, seaKernel := seaKernel,
        occupation_continuous := occupation_continuous, surfacePrimitive_continuous := surfacePrimitive_continuous,
        occupation_hasDerivAt := occupation_hasDerivAt, surfacePrimitive_hasDerivAt := surfacePrimitive_hasDerivAt,
        occupationDerivative_intervalIntegrable := occupationDerivative_intervalIntegrable,
        surfacePrimitiveDerivative_intervalIntegrable := surfacePrimitiveDerivative_intervalIntegrable,
        seaProduct_intervalIntegrable := seaProduct_intervalIntegrable, boundary_vanishes := boundary_vanishes } =
    1 + sizeOf lowerEnergy + sizeOf upperEnergy + sizeOf occupationDerivative_intervalIntegrable +
          sizeOf surfacePrimitiveDerivative_intervalIntegrable +
        sizeOf seaProduct_intervalIntegrable +
      sizeOf boundary_vanishes

Finite-band clean Bloch data with an explicitly supplied occupied spectral projector.

The projector is characterized without a global eigenvector gauge: on every Hamiltonian
eigenvector it acts as the identity below the Fermi level and as zero above it. The separate
Fermi-gap field excludes the boundary case. This is the first vertical-slice boundary; constructing
the projector from functional calculus can be added later without changing downstream topology.

∀ (hbar pMax radius angle : ℝ) (coefficients : ℝ → QuantumTheory.Transport.AngularHarmonicCoefficients ℂ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.finiteCutoffPhysicalMomentumPolarFourier hbar pMax (fun p θ => (coefficients p).eval θ)
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarPoint2D radius angle) =
    ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.momentumMeasurePrefactor hbar) *
      ∫ (p : ℝ) in 0..pMax,
        ↑p *
          (QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierZerothAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) * (coefficients p).constant +
              QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierFirstCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
                (↑(Real.cos angle) * (coefficients p).firstCosine + ↑(Real.sin angle) * (coefficients p).firstSine) +
            QuantumTheory.Transport.polarFourierSecondCosineAngularKernel (p * radius / hbar) *
              ((↑(Real.cos angle) ^ 2 - ↑(Real.sin angle) ^ 2) * (coefficients p).secondCosine +
                ↑(Real.cos angle) * ↑(Real.sin angle) * (coefficients p).secondMixed))

docString:

docString:

physical prefactor omitted. The Green-function conductivity kernel is sourced to Bastin et al.,
*J. Phys. Chem. Solids* **32**, 1811–1824 (1971),

  QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedBastinOperatorIntegrand hamiltonian current₁ current₂ energy broadening =
    -((current₁ * -QuantumTheory.Transport.retardedResolvent hamiltonian energy broadening ^ 2 * current₂ -
          current₂ * -QuantumTheory.Transport.advancedResolvent hamiltonian energy broadening ^ 2 * current₁) *

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype ι] (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData system ι) (current₁ current₂ : H →L[ℂ] H)
  (energy broadening : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedBastinSpectralTraceSum system data current₁ current₂ energy broadening =
    ∑ m,
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.stredaSpectralFactor system data QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded energy
            broadening m -
          QuantumTheory.Transport.stredaSpectralFactor system data QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced energy
            broadening m) *
        (∑ n,
            QuantumTheory.Transport.stredaSpectralFactor system data QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.retarded
                    energy broadening n ^
                  2 *
                inner ℂ (data.basis m) (current₁ (data.basis n)) *
              inner ℂ (data.basis n) (current₂ (data.basis m)) -
          ∑ n,
            QuantumTheory.Transport.stredaSpectralFactor system data QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide.advanced
                    energy broadening n ^
                  2 *
                inner ℂ (data.basis m) (current₂ (data.basis n)) *
              inner ℂ (data.basis n) (current₁ (data.basis m)))

docString:
Finite-broadening residual after removing the derivative of the chosen surface primitive from
the canonical Bastin operator integrand. Keeping this remainder distinct from the conventional
Smrčka–Středa `II` term is motivated by Bonbien and Manchon, *Phys. Rev. B* **102**, 085113 (2020),
[doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.102.085113](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.102.085113), whose symmetrized
trace decomposition avoids the overlap of the conventional `I`/`II` terms. The conventional
Smrcka--Streda `I`/`II` terminology is sourced to L. Smrcka and P. Streda, *J. Phys. C* **10**,
2153 (1977), [doi:10.1088/0022-3719/10/12/021](https://doi.org/10.1088/0022-3719/10/12/021).
No direct identification of this operator remainder with the paper's trace-level sea term is
asserted here.

docString:
Formal finite-mode free grand-partition series for Bose/Fermi exchange weight `ζ`.

For `ζ = +1` this is the bosonic product `∏ᵢ (1 - qᵢ t)⁻¹`. For `ζ = -1` it is the
fermionic product `∏ᵢ (1 + qᵢ t)`, where `qᵢ = exp(-β εᵢ)`. The proof argument deliberately
restricts this product construction to those two exchange weights.

    if ζ = 1 then ∏ i, (1 + (-ζ * Complex.exp (-↑β * ↑(ε i))) • PowerSeries.X)⁻¹
    else ∏ i, (1 + (-ζ * Complex.exp (-↑β * ↑(ε i))) • PowerSeries.X)

The actual arbitrary-occupation-space Dyson coefficient of a finitely supported bosonic quartic
interaction is a finite sum over support-valued vertex-label sequences. Each summand is a static
bare operator product multiplied by its scalar ordered-simplex Dyson coefficient.

The ambient mode type need not be finite, and no infinite Gibbs sum/integral interchange is used.

  (∀ (i : Mode), 0 < β * ε i) →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ),
      SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDysonCoeff ε β (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticInteractionOn support g) n
          t =
        ∑ q,
          SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDysonSequenceCoeff ε g (fun i => ↑(q i)) t *
            ∑ pairing,
              pairing.evaluation (Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.boson pairing)
                fun a b =>
                SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β
                  (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticFreeThermalFieldFamily (fun i => ↑(q i)) a)
                  (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticFreeThermalFieldFamily (fun i => ↑(q i)) b)

statement:
{Operator : Type u_1} →
  {s : SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics} →
    {motive : SecondQuantization.Common.BlochDeDominicis.ExpectationPairingRecursion Operator s → Sort u} →
      (t : SecondQuantization.Common.BlochDeDominicis.ExpectationPairingRecursion Operator s) →
        ((expectation : List Operator → ℂ) →
            (pairValue : Operator → Operator → ℂ) →
              (admissible : (n : ℕ) → (Fin (2 * n) → Operator) → Prop) →
                (expectation_nil : expectation [] = 1) →
                  (admissible_erase :
                      ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → Operator),
                        admissible (n + 1) C → ∀ (j : Fin (2 * n + 1)), admissible n fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ) →
                    (expectation_succ :
                        ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → Operator),
                          admissible (n + 1) C →
                            expectation (List.ofFn C) =
                              ∑ j,
                                ↑s.zetaInt ^ ↑j * pairValue (C 0) (C j.succ) *
                                  expectation (List.ofFn fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ)) →
                      motive
                        { expectation := expectation, pairValue := pairValue, admissible := admissible,
                          expectation_nil := expectation_nil, admissible_erase := admissible_erase,
                          expectation_succ := expectation_succ }) →
          motive t

∀ {Config : Type u_1} (s : SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics) (energy : Config → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
  (C :
    Fin (2 * (n + 1)) →
      SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (∃ q c,
      (∀ (i : Fin (2 * (n + 1))),
          (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) (C i) = Complex.exp ↑(q i * -β) • C i) ∧
        (∀ (i j : Fin (2 * (n + 1))),
            i ≠ j → ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator (↑s.zetaInt) (C i) (C j) = c i j • LinearMap.id) ∧
          ∀ (i : Fin (2 * (n + 1))), 1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q i * β) ≠ 0) →
    ∀ (j : Fin (2 * n + 1)),
      ∃ q c,
        (∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)),
            (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) (C (j.succAbove i).succ) =
              Complex.exp ↑(q i * -β) • C (j.succAbove i).succ) ∧
          (∀ (i j_1 : Fin (2 * n)),
              i ≠ j_1 →
                ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator (↑s.zetaInt) (C (j.succAbove i).succ) (C (j.succAbove j_1).succ) =
                  c i j_1 • LinearMap.id) ∧
            ∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)), 1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q i * β) ≠ 0

  (C :
    Fin (2 * (m + 1)) →
      SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (∃ q c,
      (∀ (i : Fin (2 * (m + 1))),
          (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) (C i) = Complex.exp ↑(q i * -β) • C i) ∧
        (∀ (i j : Fin (2 * (m + 1))),
            i ≠ j → ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator (↑s.zetaInt) (C i) (C j) = c i j • LinearMap.id) ∧
          ∀ (i : Fin (2 * (m + 1))), 1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q i * β) ≠ 0) →
    SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (List.ofFn C).prod =
      ∑ j,
        ↑s.zetaInt ^ ↑j * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C 0 ∘ₗ C j.succ) *
          SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (List.ofFn fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ).prod

  (energy : Config → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
  (C :
    Fin (2 * n) → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (q : Fin (2 * n) → ℝ) (c : Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n) → ℂ),
  (∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)),
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) (C i) = Complex.exp ↑(q i * -β) • C i) →
    (∀ (i j : Fin (2 * n)), i ≠ j → ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator (↑s.zetaInt) (C i) (C j) = c i j • LinearMap.id) →
      (∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)), 1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q i * β) ≠ 0) →
        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (List.ofFn C).prod =
          ∑ pairing,
            Combinatorics.Pairing.weight s pairing *
              ∏ pr ∈ pairing.pairs, SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C pr.1 ∘ₗ C pr.2)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.BlochDeDominicis.finiteGibbsExpectation_prod_eq_sum_pairing
docString:
**The general finite-temperature Bloch–de Dominicis theorem.** The original linked-diagram
and finite-temperature pairing development is C. Bloch and C. de Dominicis, *Nuclear Physics*
**7**, 459–479 (1958),
[doi:10.1016/0029-5582(58)90285-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(58)90285-2).
For the unified bosonic/fermionic thermal Wick argument motivating this pairing formula, see M. Gaudin, *Nuclear
Physics* **15**, 89–91 (1960),
[doi:10.1016/0029-5582(60)90285-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(60)90285-6). This theorem is
the finite-Gibbs recursion specialization described above; it does not claim the infinite-volume
or interacting-state generality of the original diagrammatic development.

  Combinatorics.allPairings 2 =
      {Combinatorics.pairingAdjacent, Combinatorics.pairingCrossing, Combinatorics.pairingNested} ∧

**The occupation-basis interface**: a Fock-space basis type `Config`, together with a
`vacuum` state and a per-mode occupation-number reading `occupation : Config → Mode → ℕ`, subject
to the physically expected constraints — the vacuum has no particles anywhere, every state has
only finitely many occupied modes, and the reading determines the state. A `class` (not a plain
`structure`) so each statistics' concrete instance is found by typeclass resolution once `Mode`
and its `Config` are fixed, rather than needing to be threaded explicitly.

                        finiteSupport := finiteSupport, ext := ext }) →

docString:
**Reconstruct a two-point diagram from an external piece and a vacuum piece.**

The external labels come from the external piece, each vertex label is read off whichever side its
vertex belongs to, and the pairing is assembled by `Pairing.ofSplit` along `slotLegSplitting`.

Nothing here inspects connectivity: the vacuum piece may be disconnected, and the external piece is
not required to be externally connected. Those conditions belong to the statement that this is
inverse to the decomposition, not to the construction.

∀ {N : ℕ} {ExternalLabel : Type u_1} {InternalLabel : Type u_2} {S T : Finset (Fin N)} (h : T ⊆ S)
  (ext ext_1 : SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram ExternalLabel InternalLabel N T),
  ext = ext_1 →
    ∀ (vac vac_1 : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram InternalLabel N (S \ T)),
      vac = vac_1 →
        SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.ofSlotSplit h ext vac =
          SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.ofSlotSplit h ext_1 vac_1
name: SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.ofSlotSplit.congr_simp

statement:
∀ {ExternalLabel : Type u_1} {InternalLabel : Type u_2} {n : ℕ} (T : Finset (Fin n))
  (ext : SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram ExternalLabel InternalLabel n T)
  (vac : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram InternalLabel n (Finset.univ \ T)) (τ τ' : ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ)
  (hσ : StrictAnti (σ ∘ SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumSlot T))
  (pr : (vac.pairingInOrder (SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumOrder T)).NormalizedPair),
  let d := SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.ofSlotSplit ⋯ ext vac;
  have q :=
    (SecondQuantization.Common.orderedLegToDiagramLeg (Finset.univ \ T)
        (SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumOrder T))
      (↑pr).1;
  d.mixedPairComponent τ τ' σ
      ((SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.slotSplitVacuumNormalizedPairEmbedding T ext vac τ τ' σ hσ) pr) =
    ⟨d.vertexGraph.componentBlock
        (SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumVertex (SecondQuantization.Common.vertexOfLeg q)),
      ⋯⟩

  (F : ℝ → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (a b : ℝ),
  (∀ (k n : Config),
      IntervalIntegrable (fun σ => SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (F σ) k n) MeasureTheory.volume a b) →
    L ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral F a b =
      SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral (fun σ => L ∘ₗ F σ) a b
name: SecondQuantization.Common.comp_operatorIntervalIntegral
docString:
**Left-composition with a fixed operator commutes with `operatorIntervalIntegral`**:
`L ∘ (∫ F) = ∫ (L ∘ F)`, given interval-integrability of every matrix coefficient `F` contributes.
Both sides reduce, via `matrixCoeff_comp`/`matrixCoeff_operatorIntervalIntegral`, to the same
`∑ k, matrixCoeff L m k * ∫ σ, matrixCoeff (F σ) k n` vs. `∫ σ, ∑ k, matrixCoeff L m k *
matrixCoeff (F σ) k n` — the finite-sum/integral interchange `intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum`
supplies, after pulling the constant `matrixCoeff L m k` in/out of each summand's integral
(`intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul`). Needed to move an already-evaluated interaction-picture
vertex factor past the ordered-simplex integral over the *remaining* Dyson coefficient.

∀ {Config : Type u_1} (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  (∀ p ∈ l, ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
    C1 ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod =
      ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l + ζ ^ l.length • (List.map Prod.fst l).prod ∘ₗ C1
name: SecondQuantization.Common.comp_prod_eq_of_zetaCommutator
docString:
**Peeling `C₁` through an arbitrary-length product**: repeatedly rewriting `C₁Bⱼ` via each
pair's `ζ`-commutator coefficient and pushing `C₁` rightward, `C₁` lands at the very end having
picked up `ζ^{l.length}`.

  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) C = Complex.exp ↑(q * τ) • C →
    SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ ∘ₗ C =
      Complex.exp ↑(q * τ) • C ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ
name: SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution_comp_eq_smul_comp_diagonalEvolution
docString:
**The KMS-type relation**: if a linear map `C` picks up an exponential eigenvalue-shift factor
`e^{qτ}` under `heisenbergEvolve` (as every `create`/`annihilate` operator does, with `q` the
eigenvalue shift `∓ε_i`), then `e^{τH₀}` and `C` satisfy `e^{τH₀} C = e^{qτ} C e^{τH₀}` — the exact
statistics-agnostic algebraic ingredient the finite-temperature Bloch–de Dominicis theorem's
KMS-rotation step needs (`ĉ_α e^{-βĤ} = e^{-βξ_α} e^{-βĤ} ĉ_α` in the project's physics reference
notes, `quantum-statistical-mechanics.tex`'s "product-of-KMS-state-and-ladder-op"), obtained purely
by rearranging the already-proved semigroup law and mutual inversion
(`diagonalEvolution_neg_comp`) — no new physical input beyond the eigenvalue-shift hypothesis
`hC`, and in particular no dependence on the concrete occupation-state type or exchange statistics.
Both `Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`/`_create` and
`Bosonic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`/`_create` supply exactly this hypothesis (with
`q := -ε i`/`q := ε i` respectively), so this single `Common/` lemma gives the KMS relation for
`create`/`annihilate` in both statistics at once.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {Config : Type u_2} (energy : Config → ℝ) (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (create annihilate :
    Mode → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (support : Finset (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode))
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
  (∀ (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →
    (∀ (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
        (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (annihilate i) =
          Complex.exp (-↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • annihilate i) →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ),
        SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff energy
            (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticInteractionOn support create annihilate g) n t =
          ∑ q,
            SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDysonSequenceCoeff ε g (fun i => ↑(q i)) t •
              SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexSequenceOperator create annihilate fun i => ↑(q i)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff_quarticInteractionOn_eq_sum
docString:
The finite-order Dyson coefficient of a finitely supported quartic interaction is the sum over
support-valued vertex sequences of their scalar ordered-simplex coefficients multiplying the
corresponding bare vertex products. This is statistics-independent once the ladder operators obey
the stated free imaginary-time eigenoperator laws.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {Config : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype Mode] (energy : Config → ℝ) (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (create annihilate :
    Mode → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
  (∀ (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
      (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →
    (∀ (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
        (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ) (annihilate i) =
          Complex.exp (-↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • annihilate i) →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ),
        SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff energy (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticInteraction create annihilate g) n
            t =
          ∑ q,
            SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDysonSequenceCoeff ε g q t •
              SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexSequenceOperator create annihilate q
name: SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff_quarticInteraction_eq_sum
docString:
On a finite mode type, the quartic Dyson coefficient is the sum over all vertex-label
sequences of the statistics-independent scalar ordered-simplex coefficient times the bare vertex
product.

∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ)
  (ζ c12 c13 c14 : ℂ)
  (C1 C2 C3 C4 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    C1 ∘ₗ C2 - ζ • C2 ∘ₗ C1 = c12 • LinearMap.id →
      C1 ∘ₗ C3 - ζ • C3 ∘ₗ C1 = c13 • LinearMap.id →
        C1 ∘ₗ C4 - ζ • C4 ∘ₗ C1 = c14 • LinearMap.id →
          1 - ζ ^ 3 * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
            SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C2 ∘ₗ C3 ∘ₗ C4) =
              (c12 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C3 ∘ₗ C4) +
                    ζ * c13 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C4) +
                  ζ ^ 2 * c14 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C3)) /
                (1 - ζ ^ 3 * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))

**The genuine normalized 2-point Bloch–de Dominicis value**: `⟨C₁Cⱼ⟩ = c₁ⱼ/(1 - ζw₁)`,

  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod) =

docString:

imaginary times `τ_A`, `τ_B`: the later time acts first (leftmost), with exchange sign
`Statistics.zetaInt s`, and the two orderings are symmetrized at equal times.

  SecondQuantization.Common.timeOrderedProduct s A B τA τB =
    if τB < τA then A ∘ₗ B else if τA < τB then ↑s.zetaInt • B ∘ₗ A else 2⁻¹ • (A ∘ₗ B + ↑s.zetaInt • B ∘ₗ A)

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      (1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β)) *
          SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock
            (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C1 ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod) =
        SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock
          (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_peel
docString:
**The trace-level peel-first identity**: `Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate`
applied to the whole remaining product `B₁⋯Bₖ` (rotating `C₁` from the end back to the front)
combined with `comp_prod_eq_of_zetaCommutator`'s operator identity, solving the resulting
self-referential equation for `Tr[e^{-βH₀}(C₁B₁⋯Bₖ)]`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q : ℝ)
  (A C : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C = Complex.exp ↑(q * -β) • C →
    SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ A ∘ₗ C) =
      Complex.exp ↑(q * β) •
        SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C ∘ₗ A)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate
docString:
**The KMS-type trace rotation**: `Tr[e^{-βH₀} (A C)] = e^{qβ} Tr[e^{-βH₀} (C A)]`, for any
operator `A` and any operator `C` with eigenvalue-shift `q` under `heisenbergEvolve`. Combines
`traceFock_comp_comm` (cyclicity) with `comp_diagonalEvolution_eq_smul_diagonalEvolution_comp` (the
KMS-type relation) exactly as the physics reference notes' `⟨Ĉ₂⋯Ĉ_{2n}Ĉ₁⟩ = w₁⟨Ĉ₁Ĉ₂⋯Ĉ_{2n}⟩` step
does.

explicit summability assumptions because Mathlib defines a non-summable `tsum` to be zero.

name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_comp_comm
docString:

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β)) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, ScalarExchange.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      (Summable fun n =>
          SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff
            (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l) n
            n) →
        Summable
            (Function.uncurry fun n k =>
              SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff
                  (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod) n k *
                SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff C1 k n) →
          (1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β)) *
              SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace
                (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C1 ∘ₗ (List.map Prod.fst l).prod) =
            SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace
              (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients ζ l)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_diagonalEvolution_comp_peel
docString:
**The `tsum` trace-level peel-first identity**: the `[Fintype Config]`-free analogue of
`traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_peel`, given the same `ζ`-commutator and KMS eigenvalue-shift
hypotheses plus explicit summability of `ScalarExchange.peelSumWithCoefficients`'s own diagonal series (`hPeel`) and of the
rotation's double series (`hRotate`). Summability of the rotated tail's diagonal series (`n ↦
(e^{-βH₀}(B₁⋯Bₖ)C₁)ₙₙ`) is *not* a separate hypothesis — it follows from `hRotate` alone via

    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDensityOperator ε β hsum).expectation
        (ScalarExchange.peelSum SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.operator
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.anticommutatorValue (-1) C₁ l) +
      (-1) ^ l.length *
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (l ++ [C₁])
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation_cons_eq_peel_add_rotated
docString: Expectation-level exchange formula before the KMS rotation of the final term.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β) (n : ℕ)
  (C : Fin (2 * n) → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsAdmissible ε β n C →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (List.ofFn C) =
      ∑ pairing,
        Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion pairing *
          ∏ pr ∈ pairing.pairs,
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum [C pr.1, C pr.2]

recursion data into the common pairing induction.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)
  (A :
    ↥(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFockSpace Mode) →L[ℂ]
      ↥(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFockSpace Mode)),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDensityOperator ε β hsum).expectation (C.operator ∘SL A) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDensityOperator ε β hsum).expectation (A ∘SL C.operator)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation_operator_comp
docString:
Completed free-Gibbs KMS rotation for one thermal ladder and an arbitrary bounded operator:
`⟨C A⟩β = gβ(C) ⟨A C⟩β`.  The scalar `gβ(C)` is the same factor appearing in
`ρβ C = gβ(C) C ρβ`.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C D : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode),
  1 + SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C ≠ 0 →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum [C, D] =
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C /
          (1 + SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C) *
        C.anticommutatorValue D

docString:

with the canonical traced Bastin energy integral.

The finite spectral current-current response equals `V (-η)` times the traced Bastin integral at
energy broadening `ℏη`, minus the contact expectation. Proving this field from a concrete Peierls
model is the remaining model-specific sum-rule problem; using the bridge below requires the field
explicitly.

  (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble) (hbar : ℝ) (hbar_pos : 0 < hbar)
  (spectralData :
    (ω : Ω) → QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData (ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω) ι)
  (convention : QuantumTheory.Transport.PositiveVolume)
  (geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E) (direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site) (q eta lowerEnergy upperEnergy : ℝ)
  (occupation : ℝ → ℂ),
  (∀ (ω : Ω),
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.FiniteStaticPeierlsWardIdentity convention
        (ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω) (spectralData ω) geometry direction K q eta lowerEnergy

          spectralData convention geometry direction K q eta =

            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction

            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
              (↑(ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω).hbar) (↑q) K)
            (QuantumTheory.Transport.kuboBastinEnergyBroadening (ensemble.configurationSystem hbar hbar_pos ω).hbar eta)

statement:
∀ {Site : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : LinearOrder Site] [inst_1 : Fintype Site] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup E]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℝ E]
  (system :

  (expectation :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E) (direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site),
  K.HasHermitianAmplitudes →
    ∀ (q ω η T : ℝ) {β M : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K))
                  s‖ ≤
              M) →
          T ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 T →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                      (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K))
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)
                    lam T)
                (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.finiteTimeAdiabaticDirectionalCosineResponse system expectation
                  geometry direction K q ω η T)
                0

The cosine quadrature is a genuine real-source response theorem. Its derivative contains the

statement:
∀ {Site : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : LinearOrder Site] [inst_1 : Fintype Site] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup E]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℝ E]
  (system :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (expectation :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (f : ℝ → ℝ) (geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E) (direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site),
  K.HasHermitianAmplitudes →
    ∀ (q : ℝ) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K))
                  s‖ ≤
              M) →
          t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 t →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K))
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)
                    (↑(f t) •
                      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K)
                    lam t)
                ((∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
                    ↑(f s) *
                      QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.retardedSusceptibility system expectation
                        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
                          (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
                        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
                          (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
                        t s) +
                  expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system
                      (↑(f t) •
                        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                          (↑q) K)
                      t))
                0

  (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
  (S : Finset α),
  SecondQuantization.Common.dysonTraceVertexMoment (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β V S =
    ↑S.card.factorial *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
        (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperatorAlgEquiv
          (SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) V S.card β))

  SecondQuantization.Common.dysonTraceVertexMoment (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) S =
    ∑ d, SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticWickDiagramAmplitude ε β g d

docString: Canonical direction of the Dyson-to-Wick-diagram expansion.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {α : Type u_2} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (S : Finset α),
  SecondQuantization.Common.dysonTraceVertexMoment (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) S =
    ↑S.card.factorial * (-1) ^ S.card *
      ∑ q,
        (∏ i, g (q i)) *
          ∑ pairing,
            intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral S.card β fun τ =>
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairingEvaluation ε β q τ pairing

docString: `Common.dysonTraceVertexMoment` of the quartic interaction in the canonical pairing-evaluator presentation.

  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ)

interaction slots and the vacuum-free external / quartic diagram pair. Only the external
factor carries the fixed-label constraint.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ)
  (externalLabel : Fin (2 * E) → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalFieldLabel Mode) (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ)
  (n : ℕ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionDysonCoefficient ε β g externalLabel externalTime n =
    ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
      ∑ T ∈ Finset.powersetCard m Finset.univ,
        ∑ p,
          if (↑p.1).externalLabel = externalLabel then
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.dysonAmplitude
              (↑((SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.externalSupportFiberEquiv ⋯).symm p)) ε β g
              externalTime
          else 0
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionDysonCoefficient_eq_sum_powersetCard_externalSupportFiber
docString:
Group the external-support fibers by their number of interaction vertices.

This is the fixed-external coefficient in the cardinality coordinates needed for the binary
external/vacuum slot-shuffle decomposition. No amplitude product is asserted here.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {E : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ)
  (externalLabel : Fin (2 * E) → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalFieldLabel Mode) (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ)
  (m k : ℕ),
  (∑ T ∈ Finset.powersetCard m Finset.univ,
      ∑ p,
        if (↑p.1).externalLabel = externalLabel then
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalInsertionWickDiagram.dysonAmplitude
            (↑((SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.externalSupportFiberEquiv ⋯).symm p)) ε β g
            externalTime
        else 0) =
    ∑ shuffle,
      ∑ q,
        have d :=
          ↑((SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.externalSupportFiberEquiv ⋯).symm
              ((SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram.standardizedSupportFiberDataEquiv shuffle).symm q));
        if d.externalLabel = externalLabel then d.dysonAmplitude ε β g externalTime else 0
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionDysonCoefficient_powersetCard_eq_sum_standardizedSupportShuffle
docString:
Fixing external order `m` and vacuum order `k`, the integrated Dyson-amplitude
support fibers can be summed in standard coordinates independent of the shuffle.

The external-label constraint and the full integrated amplitude are retained; identifying
the shuffle sum with a product of separate integrals is the subsequent analytic step.

      (PowerSeries.coeff 3)

          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β

        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 1 ^
          3

docString:
**The general theorem's `c i j` coefficient family**, for the evolved, flattened `4n`-leg
family — the product of both legs' `Complex.exp` eigenvalue-shift scalars and the Common bare

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] {n : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (q : Fin n → SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) (τ : Fin n → ℝ) (p p' : Fin (2 * (2 * n))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegCommutatorCoeff ε q τ p p' =
    Complex.exp
          ↑(τ (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n p) *
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLegEnergyShiftForSequence ε q p) *
        Complex.exp
          ↑(τ (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n p') *
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLegEnergyShiftForSequence ε q p') *
      SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticLocalLeg.exchangeCoeff SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion
        (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLeg (q (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n p))
          (SecondQuantization.Common.flatLocalLeg n p))
        (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLeg (q (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n p'))
          (SecondQuantization.Common.flatLocalLeg n p'))

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {n : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)

          ↑(τ (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n b) *
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLegEnergyShiftForSequence ε q b) *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
        (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperatorAlgEquiv
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator (q (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n a))
              (SecondQuantization.Common.flatLocalLeg n a) ∘ₗ
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator (q (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n b))
              (SecondQuantization.Common.flatLocalLeg n b)))

  (L : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
      (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperatorAlgEquiv
        (L ∘ₗ
          SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε)
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) n t)) =
    (-1) ^ n *
      ∑ q,
        (∏ i, g (q i)) *
          intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n t fun τ =>
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
              (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperatorAlgEquiv
                (L ∘ₗ
                  SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexSequenceInteractionPicture
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create
                    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate n q τ))

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionHamiltonian
docString:
**A density-density interaction Hamiltonian** for a coupling `V : Mode → Mode → ℝ`,
`H_int := Σᵢⱼ V(i,j) Nᵢ Nⱼ` — the `Common.diagonalOperator` with eigenvalue `Σᵢ∈n Σⱼ∈n V(i,j)` at
each occupation state `n`, matching `Nᵢ Nⱼ`'s eigenvalue `[i ∈ n] · [j ∈ n]` on occupation numbers.

**Summation convention, fixed explicitly since it is not forced by the physics alone:** the sum
runs over *every* ordered pair `(i, j) : Mode × Mode`, including `i = j` (contributing `V(i,i) Nᵢ`,
since `Nᵢ² = Nᵢ` on occupation numbers), with **no `1/2` prefactor** and **no assumption that `V`
is symmetric**. Consequently, for symmetric `V` this double-counts each unordered pair `{i, j}`
with `i ≠ j` (contributing `V(i,j) + V(j,i) = 2V(i,j)`) relative to the more common physics
convention `H_int = ½ Σᵢⱼ V(i,j) Nᵢ Nⱼ` (summed the same way) or `Σ_{i<j} V(i,j) Nᵢ Nⱼ`. Callers
building a specific physical model must choose `V` (and, if matching a `½ Σ` convention, halve it)
accordingly — this file makes no claim about which convention `V` follows.

This interaction is diagonal in the occupation-number basis (as `interactionHamiltonian_basisState`
shows) and hence commutes with `freeHamiltonian` and `numberOperator`. It therefore represents a
restricted density-density interaction rather than a general quartic operator
`Σᵢⱼₖₗ V(i,j,k,l) cᵢ† cⱼ† cₖ cₗ`.

  (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S) (τ : Fin S.card → ℝ) (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * S.card))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β d order τ a b =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.timedFieldPairContraction ε β
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLegFieldForSequence (fun i => d.vertexLabel (order i)) τ a)

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  {S : Finset (Fin N)} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode N S)
  (orders : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.ComponentVertexOrders d)
  (shuffle : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.ComponentShuffle d) (τ : Fin S.card → ℝ)
  (B : ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.vertexGraph d).componentPartitionOn.parts)
  (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * (↑B).card))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β d
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.assembleVertexOrder d orders shuffle) τ
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.componentOrderedLeg d shuffle B a)
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.componentOrderedLeg d shuffle B b) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.restrictComponent d ⋯) (orders B)
      (Combinatorics.FamilySlotShuffleTo.timeAssignment shuffle τ B) a b
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue_componentOrderedLeg
docString:
Pair values agree after embedding both component-local ordered legs into the assembled global
ordered-leg enumeration.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {N : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  {S : Finset (Fin N)} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode N S)
  (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S) (τ : Fin S.card → ℝ) (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * S.card))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β d order τ a b =
    Complex.exp
          ↑(τ ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).1 *
              SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegEnergyShift ε
                (d.vertexLabel (order ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).1))
                ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).2) *
        Complex.exp
          ↑(τ ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).1 *
              SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegEnergyShift ε
                (d.vertexLabel (order ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).1))
                ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).2) *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
        (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperatorAlgEquiv
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator
              (d.vertexLabel (order ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).1))
              ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).2 ∘ₗ
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator
              (d.vertexLabel (order ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).1))
              ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).2))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue_eq
docString: Closed form of a pair value after extracting the imaginary-time exponential factors.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {N : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  {S : Finset (Fin N)} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode N S)
  (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S) (τ : Fin S.card → ℝ) (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * S.card))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β d order τ a b =
    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
      (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperatorAlgEquiv
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticLegOperator ε d order τ a ∘ₗ
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticLegOperator ε d order τ b))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue_eq_freeGibbsDensityOperator_expectation
docString:
The Wick pair value is the canonical free Gibbs density-state expectation of the transported
operator product.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {N : ℕ} {S : Finset (Fin N)} (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (β : ℝ) (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode N S)
  (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram.orderedSimplexContribution ε β d order =
    intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral S.card β fun τ =>
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairingEvaluation ε β (fun i => d.vertexLabel (order i)) τ
        (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.pairingInOrder d order)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedSimplexContribution_eq_pairingEvaluation
docString:
A diagram's fixed-order ordered-simplex contribution is the integral of its canonical pairing
evaluation after transport to the chosen vertex order.

  (d : SecondQuantization.Common.ExternalInsertionDiagram ExternalLabel InternalLabel E N S)
  (blockOrder : ↥d.vertexGraph.componentPartition.parts ≃ Fin (Fintype.card ↥d.vertexGraph.componentPartition.parts))
  (pairValue : Fin (2 * (2 * S.card + E)) → Fin (2 * (2 * S.card + E)) → ℂ)
  (localPairValue :
    (B : ↥d.vertexGraph.componentPartition.parts) →
      Fin (2 * (2 * (SecondQuantization.Common.interactionSector ↑B).card + d.externalPairCount B)) →
        Fin (2 * (2 * (SecondQuantization.Common.interactionSector ↑B).card + d.externalPairCount B)) → ℂ),
  (∀ (B : ↥d.vertexGraph.componentPartition.parts)
      (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * (SecondQuantization.Common.interactionSector ↑B).card + d.externalPairCount B))),
      pairValue (d.componentDiagramLeg B a) (d.componentDiagramLeg B b) = localPairValue B a b) →
    d.pairing.evaluation (Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion d.pairing)
        pairValue =
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.componentExternalOrderSign d blockOrder *
        ∏ B,
          (d.restrictComponent B).pairing.evaluation
            (Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion (d.restrictComponent B).pairing)
            (localPairValue B)

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {i j : Mode} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)

      if

statement:

  (externalLabel : Fin (2 * E) → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.ExternalFieldLabel Mode) (externalTime : Fin (2 * E) → ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.vacuumNormalizedExternalInsertionDysonSeries ε β g externalLabel externalTime =
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.vacuumFreeExternalInsertionDysonSeries ε β g externalLabel externalTime ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalInsertionDysonCoefficient ε β g externalLabel externalTime n =
        ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.vacuumFreeExternalInsertionDysonCoefficient ε β g externalLabel externalTime m *
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) (n - m)

The vacuum-normalized arbitrary-external linked-cluster identity is equivalent to the
coefficientwise Cauchy factorization by the normalized vacuum partition coefficients.

This is a formal-series reduction, not the missing fermionic integrand factorization:
the right-hand side still requires the physical support/vacuum shuffle proof.

docString:
**The vacuum-normalized two-point series**: the two-point series divided by the partition series
of the same interaction, normalized to constant coefficient one.

The division is by the *normalized* partition series because the two-point coefficients are already
free Gibbs **expectations** — the free partition function has been divided out of each of them, so
only the interacting vacuum contributions remain to be cancelled.

    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.twoPointDysonSeries ε β g i j τ τ' *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonPartitionSeries ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g)).normalizeByConstantCoeff⁻¹

**The core Fubini computation underlying basis-independence of `innerHS`.** For `S`, `T`
Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to a basis `d`, and *any* other basis `f`, the double sum
`Σᵢⱼ ⟪S dᵢ, fⱼ⟫ ⟪fⱼ, T dᵢ⟫` (`summable_inner_resolution_product`) can be summed either row-first
(giving `Σᵢ ⟪S dᵢ, T dᵢ⟫`, via the resolution of the identity along `f`) or column-first (giving
`Σⱼ ⟪T† fⱼ, S† fⱼ⟫`, via the resolution of the identity along `d`, after rewriting each factor
with the adjoint).

docString:

`⟪S dᵢ, fⱼ⟫⟪fⱼ, T dᵢ⟫`, for `S`, `T` Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to `d` and *any* other basis

nonnegative). The absolute-summability half of

row/column identification that follows it.

statement:
∀ (side : QuantumTheory.Transport.SpectralSide) (v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenOperator✝ side v m px py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar =
    QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator
      (QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenScalarCoefficient side v m px py probeEnergy
                disorderStrength hbar •
              1 +
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x side v m
                px py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar •
              QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaX +
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y side v m
              px py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar •
            QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaY +
        QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornPauliGreenPauliCoefficient InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z side v m px
            py probeEnergy disorderStrength hbar •
          QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaZ)

statement:
∀ (axis : QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.PauliAxis) (kernel : ℝ → QuantumTheory.Models.MassiveDirac.Matrix2)
  (prefactor : ℂ) (a b : ℝ),
  (∀ (i j : Fin 2), IntervalIntegrable (fun p => kernel p i j) MeasureTheory.volume a b) →
    (match axis with
      | InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x =>
        ((prefactor * ∫ (p : ℝ) in a..b, kernel p 0 1) + prefactor * ∫ (p : ℝ) in a..b, kernel p 1 0) / 2
      | InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y =>
        Complex.I * ((prefactor * ∫ (p : ℝ) in a..b, kernel p 0 1) - prefactor * ∫ (p : ℝ) in a..b, kernel p 1 0) / 2
      | InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z =>
        ((prefactor * ∫ (p : ℝ) in a..b, kernel p 0 0) - prefactor * ∫ (p : ℝ) in a..b, kernel p 1 1) / 2) =
      prefactor * ∫ (p : ℝ) in a..b, InternalSpace.pauliVectorCoefficient (kernel p) axis

docString:
A total real-rate extension of the finite pure-point physical susceptibility.

For `eta > 0`, this is exactly
`adiabaticFrequencyDomainSusceptibilityOfPositiveRate`.  At nonpositive rates it is defined by the
same finite Lehmann expression.  This continuation is used only to package limits; all physical
statements below approach zero through positive rates.

statement:

  (data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData system ι) (A B : H →L[ℂ] H) (omega eta : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.finitePurePointPhysicalSusceptibilityExtension✝ system data A B omega eta =
    if hη : 0 < eta then
      QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticFrequencyDomainSusceptibilityOfPositiveRate system
        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointNormalizedExpectation system data) A B omega eta hη
    else ∑ mn, (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointTransitionData system data A B mn).frequencyTerm omega eta

    ∑ mn,

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  (∀ (i : Mode), 0 < β * ε i) →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ),
      SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDysonCoeff ε β (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticInteraction g) n t =
        ∑ q,
          SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDysonSequenceCoeff ε g q t *
            ∑ pairing,
              pairing.evaluation (Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.boson pairing)
                fun a b =>
                SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β
                  (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticFreeThermalFieldFamily q a)
                  (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticFreeThermalFieldFamily q b)

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  (∀ (i : Mode), 0 < β * ε i) →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode),
      True →
        SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsExpectation ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct (List.ofFn C)) =
          ∑ j,
            ↑SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.boson.zetaInt ^ ↑j *
                SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β (C 0) (C j.succ) *
              SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsExpectation ε β
                (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct (List.ofFn fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ))

  SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.IsExternallyConnected ↑ext →

name: cfc_apply_eigenvector
docString:
**The continuous functional calculus acts on eigenvectors by evaluation.** For a
self-adjoint `T` and an eigenvector `v` of `T` with (real) eigenvalue `c`, `cfc f T` acts on
`v` by scaling it by `f c`, for any continuous `f : ℝ → ℝ`. Proved by approximating `f`
uniformly by polynomials on `[-‖T‖, ‖T‖]` (a compact interval containing `spectrum ℝ T`,
via the classical Weierstrass approximation theorem) and passing to the limit using the
isometry of `cfcHom` together with Mathlib's eigenvector evaluation law for `Polynomial.aeval`.

constant coefficient, and therefore evaluate to compact operators. Compact operators are closed in

∀ {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {E : Type u_3} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] {g : ι × κ → E} {row : ι → E}
  {col : κ → E},
  Summable g →
    (∀ (i : ι), HasSum (fun j => g (i, j)) (row i)) →
      (∀ (j : κ), HasSum (fun i => g (i, j)) (col j)) →
        Summable row ∧ Summable col ∧ ∑' (i : ι), row i = ∑' (j : κ), col j
name: tsum_fiberwise_eq_of_summable
docString:
**Row-first and column-first iterated sums of a summable double family agree, with each
individually summable.** Given `g : ι × κ → E` summable, together with `HasSum` data for its row
sums (`row i = Σⱼ g(i,j)`) and column sums (`col j = Σᵢ g(i,j)`), `row` and `col` are themselves
summable and have the same total.
